comments.body: @{60285ca04963ba22994f485b|full_name} Since the tracking data and human body bones have always been inconsistent between remote and local clients and for different avatars, and we now have fallback avatar IK syncing to remote clients with some kind of normalized bone rotations for the human body bones, hopefully we're in a good position to bring some consistency to this API. If the rotations used for displaying remote fallback avatars and stuff can be calculated both locally and remotely and then provided as the rotations in udon that wouldn't be a breaking change to the API and then we would have useful body bone rotations and it would be simple to fix tracking data orientations for the remote clients hands as well.

@{6010b37283e56405c64a79b3|full_name}: yes, this is something I've looked into quite a bit. It's not a trivial problem, because unity's humanoid bone system is a bit of a black box. fallbacks work by just applying the same "muscle" data to a different avatar, which results in a similar pose. But there isn't really a good way of directly taking that muscle data and turning it into a complete, standardized position/rotation unless you were to apply that muscle data to a standardized rig. 

It is possible to use reflection to reach into the unity black box and pull out information about the current rig and the rotations needed to provided a calibrated position, but reflection is a very messy, expensive method which could break with unity updates. It's appropriate for editor scripts but better to avoid in a built game.

Another method that I've personally explored is to perform a calibration every time an avatar is loaded while they're in a T-pose, and store a relative rotation that you'd need to get from the actual bone rotation to a standardized rotation. Then when udon asks for a standardized rotation, you combine the two together. The problem with this is that not all T-poses are equal. Some avatars have overridden their T-pose to be an A-pose or even I-pose, usually for the purposes of changing how you calibrate FBT. But for the purpose of standardized calibration, that screws things up quite a bit and it would not be trivial to jam in a whole new playable layer just for a new T-pose. Additionally, some avatars have really weird bones that makes it hard to build a good standard without reaching into the unity black box. I have spent some time mostly handling that, but the more you look the more exceptions you find.
@{60285ca04963ba22994f485b|full_name}: Ahhh drats, that's much more cursed than I thought it was.

@{60285ca04963ba22994f485b|full_name}: You know, now that I think about it, I wonder if you could take the muscle data that is used for IK syncing and apply it to a standardized rig with the proportions matched to the avatar. Might be able to combine that with what you were trying to do: just load up the standard rig once during T pose, apply the same muscle positions to it that the T pose has, and then carry the offsets with the avatar. Although I don't know how the muscle positions and T pose and all that all relate so that is probably something you've looked into as well.

@{6010b37283e56405c64a79b3|full_name}: applying muscle data to a standardized rig is a lot to ask if you do it every frame for every player because you're just duplicating the amount of work, which is already quite expensive.

But only doing that once on calibration and saving the difference is a very good idea. It would completely avoid the issue of people having A or I poses, while also providing a much more "normal" standard rather than something homebrewed. I'll have to experiment with that some time to see if it would work.

details:
A deep profile of the udon VM in the engine shows a significant amount of time being spent in CheckExecutionTimeLimit. I suspect this is being called on each instruction. Since checking the high-resolution system timer can be very expensive (involving system calls, and/or a serializing RDTSC instruction), this should be avoided.
I would suggest two simple mitigations to help reduce this impact:
1. First, the execution time limit needs only be to be checked on loops - that is, on backwards branches - because otherwise, the program will eventually halt. Alternately, it could be checked every N instructions.
2. Second, the execution time limit could be checked using a less precise timer. There could be a second thread that, every second, increments a global atomic counter; the udon VM could read this counter and check against the value observed when execution began.
title: Reduce calls to CheckExecutionTimeLimit

details:
While trying to make a procedural generated map i encountered one fairly big problem when it came into syncing the generation.
When you use a seed to have the UnityEngine.Random object to generate the same values for everyone you can get the desired effect only in the current frame, from the successive frame onwards it will generate values differently from each other. My guess is that UnityEngine.Random is also used internally by vrc for other stuff, and that causes the internal state of the random generator to desync.
One solution would be to store the state of the number generator at the end of the frame and reset it at the start of the next frame, but that needs the UnityEngine.Random.State class to be exposed.
Another solution would be to Expose the System.Random class instead, since that class is not static and you can instance indepenent objects that would also avoid potential interference of UnityEngine.Random being set and reset by the user and then vrc using it internally for other reasons consequentently alterning the random generation.
title: Easier way to sync Random generators

details: RunProgram takes a uint address to start an event rather than a string event name. Right now to call methods on other behaviours, we must call SendCustomEvent which has overhead for looking up the target function's entry point in a behaviour. Exposing RunProgram would allow compilers to optimize method calls across behaviours more effectively by running a linking stage that finds the addresses of the target methods to avoid the runtime lookups of method names when possible.
title: Expose UdonBehaviour RunProgram

I'm using a while loop to increment a  private variable which is to be used to Exit the loop. The exit condition is tested against a fixed value with an  "Op Less Than" node that feeds into the bool of the While node. Even though the variable value increments up past the fixed value, the (presumed) change in state of the "Op Less Than" does not cause the While node to take the Exit path.
For comparison, I repeated the program with UdonSharp. It works correctly as expected.
Files included:
Graph and UdonSharp snapshots are attached.
You can find assets for both the Graph and the UdonSharp versions here:
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/12RfzTi6IEFK3wPsA0_LO_NpHt8YxmkFA?usp=sharing

2) Add a floor and a cube.
3) Add Box Collider and VRC Pickup to box.
4) Add Udon Behavior to cube and set Program Source to LoopTest.
5) Build & Test.

Original post:

Okay, so I decided to start using the SDK3 for making new worlds and decided to start with a simple home world. I made the place kind of big with lots of trees and plants and a house. The file size ended up a pretty standard 200 something MB. Performance wasn't great so I went back in and made the world smaller. The world had less stuff in it over all, but when I went to check it out, the performance was even worse and the file size had tripled to a whopping *600 MB.* I thought maybe I was putting to many trees in, so I made it even smaller, with far less objects in it. After uploading it the file size was now nearly 1,000 MB!! I didn't bother letting it load in. 
At this point I went and looked in the bug reports and some people were saying that Udon SDK3 scans all objects in the project at run time, and I wondered if that was the cause of the issue. So I decided to clean out anything I wasn't using from the project files in hopes of making it small again. This didn't really do anything as it stayed around the same file size even after crunching more textures.
So this time I decided to drastically reduce the amount of light probes by nearly half and I cleared out the dynamic objects and dynamic materials again because they had reset themselves. I rebaked the lightmaps and double checked I didn't have anything hidden in the map. This time I didn't even bother with a play test in Unity. Despite my best efforts, this only reduced the file size by about 9 MB, bringing it to a total of **939 MB.** My world is only a 200x200 terrain piece with a house. It shouldn't be this big. 
As a last resort, I uploaded the world again with a new blueprint ID, deleting the old version. This only reduced it to 918 MB. Once again I decided to reduce the amount of light probes. I rebaked the lighting. The file size stayed the same. At this point I have no idea what is causing the file size issues except maybe the SDK is uploading everything in the project and maybe more stuff that I'm not aware of, like maybe the GI cache?
TLDR: File size is like 10 times bigger than it should be and there's almost no way to reduce it.

details:
Now that web connectivity will likely require some form of consent from the user when using Udon, I think it's a reasonable request to ask for an actual unique user ID that we can use to identify users. This could be used to do things like enable a debug console in the world, or when web connectivity is back, save progress or settings in a world.
Right now people are using display names as "unique" identifiers which isn't good and already has issues since it's a display name. One issue is https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/onplayerjoined-doesnt-get-full-displayname-for-steam-users 
Another issue is that "special" characters like "." get replaced in the display name with lookalikes which breaks string comparisons. 

Relying on display name to "uniquely" identify people will become more prevalent as time goes on and people make commonly used systems that depend on them. You should expose this sooner rather than later to avoid this issue.

The potential for abuse is obviously possible, but there's no reason to kneecap the systems and introduce potential issues by leaving only display names visible. Right now I can reasonably target people with just their display names, it's just possible that there will be some more people with the same name that get targeted. Worlds abusing names to harass people is something that should be reported on a world basis.
title: Expose unique user IDs to Udon

details:
Currently, Udon makes "security checks" on runtime, but instead of checking an array once, it checks each element of an array whenever you access _one_ element in that array, causing exponential execution times for even the smallest arrays.
This causes huge permance issues whenever you use arrays, forcing you to write super ugly code that works without them whenever possible.
But: This UdonVM behaviour makes no sense from a security perspective. When I _create_ and _fill_ an array in Udon on runtime of a known/whitelisted type (e.g. a Vector3), there is no need to check whether or not this array is still secure when I read from it again. UdonVM needs to check an UdonBehaviour _once_ for secure/whitelisted content, not every time it is run. The whole overhead of runtime security checks shouldn't exist in a VM that only supports a set of whitelisted components.
Right now, making more complex things in Udon that rely on running in Update() is especially frustrating because it always runs fine in the editor (as it should) while it runs on 1 fps in vrchat. And this is only because you need to loop once through a few local arrays of whitelisted components with 30 elements each.
The only workaround right now is to use hundreds of class variables instead of arrays to get your frametime back. The code is unreadable at this point and coding for VRChat becomes a pain.
title: Improve runtime performance for arrays

When using Immobilize(), the whole point is that the player can't move anymore, e.g. so that users can type text on the keyboard without accidently moving when hitting WASD etc.
Currently, only WASD is blocked correctly, but a lot of other movements are not blocked. Those are jumping, crouching, laying down. Please  add those to the blocked movements so that players are not annoyed by accidental movement when they type text into an input field.
title: Immobilize() doesn't fully immobilize player

details:
Most functions that rely on avatar bones and player height need to update their calibration values when the user loads a different avatar, after the new avatar has fully loaded. This can currently only be done with expensive update loops and a lot of bone checks / measurements and therefor CPU spikes while consumes unnecessary ressources. 
An event/function for that would greatly improve performance and user experience at the same time and the world can be instantly adjusted to the new avatar (height of buttons, dealing with limited amount of finger bones etc.)
A function like OnAvatarChanged() or OnAvatarLoaded() should be called when an avatar of LocalPlayer finished loading, also on map start and each time the avatar changed.
title: Add OnAvatarChanged() event

details:
Since bone transforms aren't exposed, we can't parent objects to players and need to use expensive and complicated update loops for such a basic task, which also results in ugly/janky object movements and low performance. 
Please give us a simple function like .SetParent(Transform t, Boolean b) for .GetTrackingData(VRCPlayerApi.TrackingDataType.x) and .GetBonePosition(HumanBodyBones.x) and for VRCPlayerApi.GetPosition
title: Allow parenting objects to player bones, player position and player tracking data

This world currently only contains one UdonBehaviour which is an "Empty" Graph on a  VRC_Pickup that has "Synchronize Position" checked.

HOWEVER THIS BUG EFFECTS ALL WORLDS INCLUDING SDK2!

Every player that joins the world via direct means* will see the master as the owner of the pickup, regardless of whether someone else has become owner, before they joined.

*This can be either via launch parameters that you set to a specific instance that already contains players, or via the website features/join links. This seems to be what causes the issue. To reproduce the problem join the instance with two clients and wait until they have fully loaded. Let the client who has joined last (non-master) pickup the cube. Then join the instance with a third client. Now the third client will see the master as the owner of the pickup, despite the first and second client seeing the second client as the owner. details:
Thanks for checking out this new version of the Graph UI. You can install it using the link below - please do a CLEAN install - close Unity, delete your library and the existing Udon folders (Udon, VRChat Examples and VRCSDK) and then import the new package.
 
There's lots to see! Please take a look and file your findings - bugs, features and suggestions.

Feel free to upload and test things with this SDK, this should all work on Live with the provided SDK. 

Make sure to save your projects separately! New graphs should be mostly backwards-compatible, but no guarantees. The new Comments and Groups will not appear in the old Graph.
 
To open the New Graph, you can find it under VRChat SDK > New Graph or on an UdonBehaviour with the 'Open New Udon Graph' button. You can still access the old graph for now - this will be removed for public release.
Existing Udon bugs will not be any different, this is purely an upgrade to the Graph Window that should make it easier to use, and enable lots of great future upgrades (SubGraphs, etc). We want to test that existing graphs open and compile well with this UI, and that building new graphs works as expected. We're happy to hear about suggested features along with bugs.

SDK Link: https://files.vrchat.cloud/sdk/VRCSDK-UDON-2020.06.04.14.15_Closed_Community_Test.unitypackage
 
What's New:
 
New UI Elements

* Variables are part of a floating window now. You can create, rename and delete them right in this window (they will not show up as nodes). You can drag and drop from the window to your graph to create a 'Get Variable' node or use Search to get Set Variable nodes. We also use a text-matching search function when choosing variable types rather than the long list.
* Groups - create through right-click, drag-and-drop to add items inside.
* Comments - now standalone items created through right-click with adjustable size.

UI Improvements

* Zoom! Just roll your mousewheel!
* Visible Compilation state - check out the box in the upper-right of the graph screen. It will flash green when compiling successfully, and red when unsuccessful. Click on the box to show/hide the latest assembly or errors.
* Ports are easier to connect now
* Copy+Paste Improvements - new nodes appear around mouse
* Welcome screen for messages, known issues and settings
* Right-Click to add Nodes
* Alt+click to drag as well as middle-mouse
* Drag and Drop GameObjects from your Hierarchy to a graph to create a new Public Gameobject variable.
* New StyleSheet system - This is lower-priority, but you will be able to reskin the graph. You can see an example by turning on 'Use Neon Style' in the Settings, this will apply 'UdonGraphNeonStyle.uss' over the existing graph. Do poke around if you're curious. Don't spend time customizing this yet - we're likely to change the names and classes of some elements as part of cleanup so your custom styles will break. We'll let you know when this is locked and add an easy way to apply your own stylesheet.
 
Search
* There's now a few ways to search. Press spacebar to open up Quick Search, which will give you access to a few special commonly used nodes like Events, Debug, UdonBehaviour, as well as the Classes for other nodes like GameObjects, Ints, Networking, etc. If you pick a node from the list, it will appear. If you pick a Class, then you'll get a new search window focused on that class.
* If you want to open up the old full-search, you can do that with Tab - it will be as slow as it used to be, but should work the same.
* If you press space with an existing node selected, you will search within that node's class. So with GameObject Get Name selected, you'll see all the accessible properties and methods for GameObject when you press space. If you don't like this, you can turn it off in Settings ('Focus Search on Selected Node')

details:
`CustomEvent` could be fired by other UdonBehaviour before `Start` is fired. So, Udon programmer who implements this CustomEvent must check already initialized or not before CustomEvent body (and do initialize if needed). It's inconvenient and waste of time (in the meaning of both run-time and writing-time of users).
I prefer to do Start before CustomEvent if it's not done yet. All of the above is same for SendCustomNetworkEvent case.
(This might be a "feature request" but I chose "bug report" section because I guess this is not intended implementation.)
SDK Version: VRCSDK3-UDON-2020.05.12.10.33

--- Details
In UdonBehaviour.cs, Udon `Start` event is fired in C# `Update` methods.
Events other than SendCustomEvent and SendCustomNetworkEvent have `if(!_hasDoneStart)` check at the beginning. So it is guaranteed that Start is fired before these events in Udon program. On the other hand, SendCustomEvent does RunProgram without `_hasDoneStart` guard.
My request is inserting same thing, that C# Update method does, into SendCustomEvent. `if(!_hasDoneStart)... RunProgram(startPoint) ...`
title: Start event should be fired before processing CustomEvent and SendCustomNetworkEvent

details:
First: it attempts to place the nodes at the cursor. The way it does that is by picking one specific node and puts that at the cursor, then all the other nodes will be arranged around that as if they are children of it. The problem is that the node it picks is completely unpredictable. It's not random, but it appears to be the first according to some index. Because of the unpredictability, you have no idea where your nodes are going to go.

Second: once you have pasted a bunch of nodes, they are by default not selected.

These two issues combined means that it is very common to duplicate a group of nodes and they end up mashed together with a different group, so your only option is to undo and paste it somewhere else.
title: Pasting/duplicating has a couple of small QOL issues

details:
I can't speak for in-game performance, but in editor having OnGUI registered to every UdonBehaviour makes up a majority of the runtime overhead of empty behaviours. If I have 2000 UdonBehaviours in the scene with the Empty graph behaviour, it takes approximately 20ms on the CPU. Around 18.5ms of that overhead is from OnGUI. OnGUI also generates 0.7MB of garbage per frame for all of those events. Also note that OnGUI can run multiple times per behaviour.

Udon doesn't currently expose any IMGUI functions as far as I can see, so there isn't really a point in registering the OnGUI event in the first place.
title: Remove the OnGUI event from UdonBehaviours

details:
Currently (VRCSDK-UDON-2020.06.04.14.15_Closed_Community_Test),
dragging connecting port of a node is released on where valid port doesn't exist, it does nothing. (In other words, it cancels the edge creation).
I suggest it opens focused-search in such case, of course with appropriate focus. And it will be useful if it connect nodes automatically after search result is selected and it creates new node.
---- Detail
Use case:
1. Assuming there is a node with a output port typed `string`.
2. You drag this port and release it on free area. 
3. Graph Editor opens search window with focusing `System.String`.
4. You choose one of method from the searched list. For example `Contains`
5. Graph Editor create `Contains` node, and connects the port to instance input port of `Contains` node.
I think this behaves like auto completion in text-based programming.
1. Input variable-name and separator (dot if in C#)
2. Do auto-complete operation, select a method
3. The programming tool inserts method name
If the port is control flow, node's type can be used as the type for focusing.
However, there will be some "irregular" situations. for example:
* In the case of the node denotes an Event, then focusing to Event is useless.
* When the port is input port, then current focusing is not suitable. Maybe best way is filtering method with output type. This type of filtering is not implemented.
* When the port is output port and typed bool, it will useful if "Branch" is on the list.
So in some cases, not focused search might be better. (Or modifier key to select search style?)
title: [Suggestion] Open focused-search when new-edge-drag is released on free area

details:
Add ability to specify additional user defined styles (Unity style sheets) for the Graph.
Motivation:
When you fill comment node text with Japanese characters, currently it shows the text with a font for Chinese. This font is not good for Japanese users. (Maybe it is simplified Chinese font named <edit>"Microsoft YaHei"</edit>. Maybe it is used as fallbacks of default font "Fonts/Lucida Grande.ttf".) 
But if it specifies Japanese font, then it's not good for Chinese users. Most best way is handling language information with text as a rich text. But I think it's too much for this tool. Instead, if this tool has ability to specify font file, it's enough for most cases.
To achieve this, easier and generic way is specifying styles by users. So I suggest to support user defined styles.
(technically It's possible to solve it by modifying UdonGraphStyle.uss in SDK3. Of course, SDK modification is not allowed for user by TOS. Generally speaking, "technically possible things" sometimes spread out involuntarily. And it is bad educational thing for beginners, I think. So please provide us a legal way.)

It also seems like the player's gravity is applied during `Update()` or `LateUpdate()` instead of `FixedUpdate()`?
I'm pretty sure it belongs into `FixedUpdate()`. That caused some issues when I was trying to control the player's velocity, which I cannot do in `Update()` to keep things in sync with the physics system.

To add to this, anything 0 or below 0 won't work. While it does slow gravity, it doesn't fully stop it. 0 and -10 both act the same. However if you set the gravity strength to an absurdly low number still above 0, like 0.000001 it effectively stops gravity

details:
Right click on a node to show context menu changes node selection to that node properly. But this happens only once.
Reproduce steps:
1. Prepare three nodes.
2. Select 1st node.
3. Right click on 2nd node. Then the selection changes to 2nd node.
4. Right click on 3rd node. Then the selection remains on 2nd node. If you do delete operation, it deletes 2nd node not 3rd.
* If you right click on free area of the graph on step 3, this issue also happens.
--- Details
Probably this is a bug on Unity side. ClickSelector on the node seems not to be called.
If you select Copy operation on step 3, then this issue doesn't happen. So, system implementation of cancelling context menu have a problem, I guess.
title: Right click to show context menu changes node selection but only once

comments.body: I see this but I'm not sure that we'd want to change it, this is a pretty complex behaviour that's implemented on Unity's side. There are cases where you may want to change the selection on right-click, and cases where you might not. We can call out that right-click mostly works on selected nodes, so make sure you've selected what you want to modify first.

details:

details:
When a Group has multiple nodes and all of them selected, `Remove From Group` operation on the contextual menu item removes only half of nodes. The other half remains.
--- Details
The menu item handler in UdonGraph, it iterates selectedUdonNodesInGroups. Its length (or `Count()`) decrese within that loop. 
So I think `.ToList()` after `Where()` (or backward for-loop on selectedUdonNodesInGroups) is needed.

details:

comments.body: Added a special exception for IUdonEvent Receiver to allow its connection from any Component. We can now make this graph without jumping to 'T' overload and back:

Just by curiosity, I dug what's going on.
* Loading and pasting of previously created noodles are possible.
* Output port of `UnityEngineComponent.__GetComponent__T` is typed `UnityEngine.Object`. "Instance" port of `SendCustomNetworkEvent` is typed `VRC.Udon.Common.Interfaces.IUdonEventReceiver` So it isn't connectable. (because not assignable each other)
* If output port is typed `System.Object`, they are connectable. So new Graph Editor's type system itself seems to be fine.
* Old (current live) editor `UdonGraph.CanConnect(Slot fromSlot, Slot toSlot)` returns `true` if `(fromSlot.node.name.Contains("__T") || fromSlot.node.name.Contains("__TArray"))` . So it is connectable. (This should be at least endWith imo)
* Series of GetComponent methods seems to be the only cases that have parameterized output type with generics among defined nodes.

comments.body: Not sure when, but this was fixed. All primitive types are now supported including UInt64.

Is there any update on this bug? Using ulong with bit shifting is super efficient for sending more networked data without bogging it down or reaching the networking limits.
Most worlds are going to have to send twice as much network data because of this bug forcing us to use less efficient data types.
I wrote a significant amount of code I spent all day on, only to find out this data type no longer works.
Tested on the latest SDK version as of Jan 12 2021: VRCSDK3-WORLD-2020.12.09.04.44_Public

This appears to still be the case. At least it was for me. I can get normal int64 / long to work fine though. It also works for unsigned 32-bit integers. It seems to only be unsigned 64-bit (ulong) that fails.
I also see that same log message when encountering the issue.
This is on the current Udon SDK release, with the current non-beta client.
SDK used: VRCSDK3-WORLD-2020.08.07.18.18_Public.unitypackage

Adding a few details: The sending side is always the instance master and there are no errors at all on master-side. Client-side is only reading the value and completely fails to do so for all our test-users, every time the master changes the value. Client side never attempts to change this value, the error message from VRChat with "encode" in it is a bit misleading. We've used the lates Client, latest SDK, latest version of UdonSharp.

details:
If you name your GameObject `PlayerManager`, then execution of SendCustomNetworkEvent is blocked. This behavior newly started from build 944 or 946 without any notice.

I made a world for reproduction: https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_f17d2b37-2f60-47d2-b280-e4489ba29368

---
I use identical Udon program for two GameObjects. You'll see logs for the failure case (named `PlayerManager`) like this ("naqtn" is my user name):
[Network Processing] RPC called PlayerManager:UdonSyncRunProgramAsRPC:All and 10 bytes
[VRC_EventDispatcherRFC] SendRPC/AlwaysUnbuffered on PlayerManager blocked for naqtn (local master owner)

---
On the other hand, the log success case (named `Foo`) is like this:
[Network Processing] RPC called Foo:UdonSyncRunProgramAsRPC:All and 10 bytes
[VRC_EventDispatcherRFC] Will execute SendRPC/AlwaysUnbuffered on Foo (UnityEngine.GameObject) for naqtn: S: "UdonSyncRunProgramAsRPC" I: 0 F: 0 B: Unused (local master owner)
[Network Processing] RPC invoked UdonSyncRunProgramAsRPC on Foo for naqtn
[UdonSync] Foo executing echo at the behest of naqtn

---
I guess "real" PlayerManager exists somewhere (perhaps in hidden player object) and the system wants to block malicious incoming messages. It might reach with adjusted network id. But I think blocking by the name is not reliable and is not good way to do that. Because VRC_EventDispatcherRFC must be able to get the object reference of real PlayerManager internally.
I'm not sure this is a bug or intended feature. If this is a feature, please describe in the document and announce to Udon creators.
title: SendCustomNetworkEvent does not work on an object named PlayerManager

comments.body:
A note for anyone having this problem still-
Apparently this also blocks SendCustomNetworkEvent on children of the PlayerManager too.
I can just name my object "Player Manager" instead though it would have been nice to know this. Glad I found this bug report

details:
In many graph languages these days, they include a "portal" feature to help with unwieldy, complex, and long graphs. 

With the new addition of groups, it is very useful for organizing complex graphs, however, the issue arises when you want to use outputs of these groups to other groups or sections of functionality. This would in effect create long and unsightly noodle connections which are hard to manage, harder to read, harder to understand, and more error prone because of that. If you have to ask yourself, "what is this connecting to?", because it's off of the screen, it's a bad sign.

Portals solve these issues by allowing the output of one node to effectively enter a "portal", and it can connect to the same named exit portal which then connects to a nodes input, all while hiding the noodle and at the same time telling you which portal it is, thus allowing you to know where it's coming from without following a really long noodle connection.
In my opinion, Gaea did it the best, as can be seen below.
title: Udon graph portals - For organizing complex graphs

details:
If you use a Slider and set onValueChanged to go to UdonBehaviour.SendCustomEvent, it will always send 0 even though your custom event implemented a float parameter.

The reason for this is that SendCustomEvent takes a string parameters, not a float parameter, and is therefore shown under the static section, and not under the dynamic floats section. As a result, we can't actually get the float value from the callback, leaving the Slider onValueChanged event basically useless if we want to know what value it is.

A workaround would involve passing in the Slider as a public variable, then using the callback with SendCustomEvent, and grabbing the value from the Slider component.

Not entirely sure of a good solution to the problem as SendCustomEvent would always require a string parameter so it knows where it's going. Even if custom parameters were added so you can call the function with parameters, this probably still wouldn't fix it

Not sure whether you can consider this a bug or not due to the cause, but it kinda effectively behaves like a bug
title: Unity Slider onValueChanged sends 0 float

Udon version `2020.04.30.18.46`
`VRCSDK3-UDON-2020.06.11.14.01_Public.unitypackage`
The argument `float breakForce` of `OnJointBreak` event is always zero.
I used the uGUI for convenience and tested it as the following 1st figure.
I think this is because the argument name generated by the Udon assembler and the symbol name referenced by the Udon VM are mismatched.
The former is `"onJointBreakBreakForce"` but the latter is `"onJointBreakForce"`.
`"onJointBreakForce"` comes from the fact that the tuple, the first element of the second argument passed to the RunEvent method at line 360 ​​of `UdonBehaviour.cs`, is `"force"`. Correctly, it should be `"breakForce"` (2nd figure).
The same thing applies to `OnAnimatorIK` event, but the following reason, `OnAnimatorIK` doesn't work in the first place.

details:
Using SDK VRCSDK3-UDON-2020.07.16.10.33_Public.unitypackage it is now not possible to set object reference fields to null in the inspector. This happens on both Udon Graph programs and Udon Sharp programs. 
An easy repro is to put a public gameobject field on an Udon program and set it to reference some object in the scene. If you select the field and press delete the field will no longer get set to null whereas it did in the previous live Udon release. 
This issue traces back to a small change that happened on line 186 of UdonProgramAsset.cs where a null check was added before setting variable values that prevents you from setting null to any public variable from the inspector. This null check should be removed.
Specifically this line:
`if(!publicVariables.TrySetVariableValue(exportedSymbol, variableValue))`
was changed to:
`if(variableValue != null && !publicVariables.TrySetVariableValue(exportedSymbol, variableValue))`
and should be reverted
title: Unable to set object references to null in Udon behaviour inspector

details:
Unity stores the position values of GameObjects in single-precision floating-point format. This works well for small values, which it can represent precisely; but precision decreases as values increase because of floating-point rounding errors. As a result, GameObjects rendered far from the origin (0,0,0) aren't positioned accurately (they're slightly misplaced). The effect becomes more pronounced the further the gameplay moves from the origin, and it's most noticeable during animations. So for example, instead of the player moving smoothly through the scene, their movement appears jittery.
We need a floating origin solution that shifts the world when the player is x units away from the origin. Alternatively let us do it ourselves with a "unsynced" teleport remote player. I hope you understand.
Right now world size is limited to 4-5000 units in any direction, which is too small esepcially if you are doing for example a space world, racing game, etc.
title: Floating Origin

details:
I know this sounds dumb but please hear me out. The creation of Udon#, while absolutely incredible for programmers, has severely stinted development into the Udon graph system.
The issue is that the vast majority of people using Udon are only using U#, so a lot of the feedback and bug reports are coming from U# users. This has lead to huge flaws in the Udon graph system getting barely any attention and falling to the wayside.
As an example, Udon graphs had a bug where for no apparent reason, the graph would fail to compile. There would be no error and no way to tell it was broken until you tested it. Once you knew it was a broken, the only way to fix it was to duplicate it and delete the old one. This wasn't rare either, it happened almost every single time. This lead to many situations where you were left wondering if you made a mistake in the graph, or if it was just broken for no reason. This bug alone was directly responsible for everyone moving to U# development instead because it was so debilitating. It was reported on the canny early on but wasn't actually fixed until about 10 months later. This, in my opinion, is absolutely ridiculous. There is no way a bug that bad should have been left alive for so long. Anybody that used Udon graphs for more than 20 minutes should have run into this issue, so why wasn't it fixed earlier?
Udon# didn't have this issue, it was exclusive to graphs. I can only assume that the majority of the development team working on Udon was also using U# and didn't even know the bug existed.
The crux of the issue is that if development continues to be focused on Udon# instead of graphs, a lot of people new to world creation are going to be turned off about using Udon if basically everything is designed around U#. A lot of new creators don't have any programming experience and aren't going to learn an entire programming language just to make their own home world. The community stands to lose a lot of potential talent if graphs simply aren't being developed, tested, and bug fixed.
In essence, I'd just like more focus to put on graphs instead of U# getting all the attention. If graphs aren't maintained properly then the barrier of entry into world creation becomes monumental for newbies and will only encourage more content to be created on SDK2. Please remember that the only reason you don't see a lot of Udon graph issues on the canny is because people either get fed up and move to U# or just completely give up on trying to make it work. Making graphs more user and beginner friendly is absolutely essential if you want the community to move away from SDK2.
title: Put more focus on Udon graph development

details:
One of the major hurdles with using node editors is speed of development. To work well the editor must be fast and provide ample shortcuts and other speed up tools.
UE4 blueprint / material editor are nice examples of how you can make trivial tasks like branching or variable creation much nicer.
Allowing user to hold some button alongside pressing the mouse to create a particular node like a branch or a block.
UE4 Material editor (or Unity's Amplify) also allow to create a variable in place by holding a numeric key. I think it would be pretty useful if we could do something like:
1 + left click: create bool in place
2 + left click: create float in place
3 + left click: create Vector3 in place
0 + left click: create int in place
and so on. Adding a vairable and dragging it over takes some time, so that would definitely allow for faster iteration cycle.
As a sidenote in the creation - it would be nice to be able to convert a constant into a variable with some button / right click menu. [Here's a canny for that](https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/conversion-of-constants-into-variables)
UE4 shortcut lists:
[Blueprint Editor](https://docs.unrealengine.com/en-US/Engine/Blueprints/UserGuide/CheatSheet/index.html)
[Material Editor](https://odederell3d.blog/2019/12/26/ue4-material-blueprint-shortcuts/)

details:
When i am trying use Textasset file (it's just text file) with a lot video links inside, i found out it's set as String.
I discovered and now i understand there is protection built inside Udon(Sharp) where String cannot used in videoplayer or in pictures (when VRC_Panorama alternative is ready) so i am searching for solutions.

I need find a way to make it Url variable, but Udon has nothing for String conversion. There is no String to VRCUrl, but there is VRCUrl to String conversion (kinda weird). The protection is meant to avoid changing urls in runtime (in world) and send data to servers - with IP and UserID for example. That is why String is blocked. But Url works like String... so how about this?

The VRCUrl can only added in Unity in fixed Urlinputfields but i saw you can make arrays with like VRCUrl[] or VRCUrl[][]. Arrays are allowed, but manual work to add so many urls in Unity Inspector is really frustrating work. Really waste of hours work. Why can it not bit automated?

There is with InspectorGUI conversion possible with UnityEditor, but i saw it's pretty hard and not easy to understand for people who just started to learn in Udon. Even i am more in coding, it's still hard and also it's pretty dirty way for me...

The good thing about Textasset is they are read-only, because Udon cannot change Text files. So i am thinking, why not add new function TextassetUrl to Udon? It's still safe and it's way much easier to code in Udon(Sharp) because it is directly converted in Url variable (similar like String).
Then it's easy task to split it in arrays, and then we can send it to videoplayer.
But due security part, there might some rules:
- You can use + in VRCUrl, but not with String values. It stays purely in VRCUrl. Like Filename = Serverurl + filename. Serverurl is also fixed value in Udon as VRCUrl value. Count up is not possible because Int to VRCUrl is not possible. You can still add numbers but only as fixed VRCUrl value. (But it's also possible to not allow + for VRCUrl if you dont want add too much. - means all links in Textasset must full links.)
- It's not possible change or convert dynamically in VRCUrl value, because there are no Url functions.
- The only allowed function for VRCUrl is Split function to make arrays possible (and still safe because it don't add new things)
- I guess the Split(value) may used as String or Char, because the risk is very low because it cannot add new things.
- Alternative you can add SplitUrl(value) if you want make it purely for VRCUrl, where value must in VRCUrl value. If you just make sure nothing will changed. You can set VRCUrl value like private VRCUrl splitValue = "\n" and it should stay safe.

If you add new functions like TextassetUrl, i am sure many people will happy it makes way much easier to make video listings and picture listings. With Text file, it is very easy to make listings (they can made from Excel CSV export for example) and text files are packed inside World package when uploaded to the server. There is no risk something will changed in runtime. It's all fixed anyway.
BTW it's in the end identical like VRCUrl[] or VRCUrl[][] after splitting text file. (reading with TextassetUrl.Text is directly in VRCUrl variable) So there are no differences because the outcome is same.

Without this function, it's really hard to program correctly and it's also not inside Udon possible, because Textasset output is unsafe String, and that is not possible for videoplayers and VRC_Panorama (image) loading. Please make this possible. I dont like kinda dirty work with #if !COMPILER_UDONSHARP && UNITY_EDITOR function. Make it in Udon and it's much easier and much shorter code. And it looks also more clean.
title: Make TextAssetUrl possible.

details:
People have exploited Udon and are able to remotely call every defined function on other clients using SendCustomNetworkEvent. This gives those users a lot of power that they shouldn't have, especially since literally everything in Udon is public and has a network ID.
Easy fix: Create a tag like [Networkable] that must be defined for every function that is supposed to be triggered via network event. This would also reduce network IDs.
To further improve security, functions/methods and fields in Udon should respect the private/public declaration and should be unable to get accessed from outside this behavior when they are not declared as public. They should also have arbitrary names so that a modded client doesn't have a human-readable list of them.
title: Fix Udon Security Vulnerability (illegal network function calls via modded clients)

details: Currently, SetOwner takes effect after a delay. details:
I am well aware of a post that's already talking about instantiating GameObjects/Prefabs that contain UdonBehaviours, however I have dug a bit deeper to understand the cause.

Essentially what's causing the crash is the PhotonView ID being duplicated and I assume trying to replace its self.
You can notice this error if you add the Prefab to the scene and try to instantiate while using the debug logger. I attached an image showing the log error.
I noticed that you can still call methods, get variables, etc within the Prefab after you instantiate it by getting its class using the following.

'ClassName variable = (ClassName)prefabObject.GetComponent(typeof(UdonBehaviour))'

However I have noticed that some events such as Collisions (in my case) will be the death of the script whenever they occur.
A way to get around this bug (at least somewhat) is to have the prefab in the scene (nest it in an empty or something), set its active to false, then in your instantiation method for that prefab, set its active to true after you have instantiated it. You can even do it within the prefab if you call a method within it's behavior class.

Additional reference to the bug can be found here: https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/587-instantiated-prefabs-dont-have-udon-behaviours-when-in-vrc-not-editor

- SDK3 2020.11.30.20.04
- UdonSharp v0.18.8
title: PhotonView ID Duplication By Insantiation Causes UdonBehaviour's To Crash.

For example, on the UdonBehvaior -> SendCustomEvent node, the input for the udon behavior reference implicitly fills the input with the reference to the current script if the input has no connection. details:
When an event has been fired, it should be possible to query the state of the event including:
- The source of the event (Local via SendCustomEvent or built-in events like Interact, Collision, etc, or Remote for network calls via SendCustomNetworkEvent)
- The object that fired the event (or null if not relevant to the event)
- The player that fired the event (LocalPlayer or null if the event source is local)
- The name of the event (should return the internal name of the event for built-in events (e.g. Interact would return "_interact", or the name of the custom event)
- Additional parameters that were passed to the event (may provide a more flexible alternative to retrieving custom event parameters)

details:
Here's a scenario to explain what happens:
Object has a synced int.
Player 1 takes ownership of object and sets the synced int to 5. Everybody else sees 5.
Player 2 takes ownership of object and sets the synced int to 10. Everybody sees 5 turning into 10
Player 3 takes ownership of the object without changing anything. Everybody else sees 10 turn into 5, and then a moment later it's back to 10.
This is not an issue with precise timing, as it can happen even if the object has been 10 for several minutes. Somewhere, player 3 remembers that the object used to be 5 and it is interpolating into 10 or something, even if syncmode is none.
title: When taking ownership of an object, remote players will be given outdated udon synced data

details:
I would like a way to mark stations as "local" which prevents stations from doing their own internal "seated" player tracking. This allows us to reuse 1 station for all custom world locomotion systems.
Currently stations have their own special handling for making sure that late joiners see a specific person sitting in a station that they were sitting in prior. This handling also prevents you from sitting in a station if your client thinks someone else is already in it. However, if two players enter the same station at the same time, locally they will both be registered as being in the station which means the lock out provided by VRC does not guarantee anything and is essentially useless in practice for much more than a chair that's there for aesthetics since it's trivial to break unintentionally and by extension break any systems that depend on it. Anything involving stations has historically been bug prone and liable to break subtly at the drop of a hat. When issues have been fixed, they have been liable to regress a patch or two later and then get left for months or years. The same goes for the implicit syncing behaviour of stations.
Putting aside bugs with station sync aside, even if it worked perfectly 100% of the time, there are many cases where people want to implement their own locomotion in worlds which requires absolute control over the player position and rotation locally. But at the same time does not require a "vehicle" that the player is in and directly attached to.
As far as I have heard from VRC staff, stations are the supported way to do this since we cannot control the exact position of the player, only the derivative of it (the velocity), which is janky at best, and we cannot rotate the player on any other axis than Y because the player controller is not made to work correctly with any rotation off the Y axis outside of the context of stations.
On the other side, we should also be able to locally assign a remote player to a local station. Many worlds have used this to control the local perception of the location of remote players. Allowing for non-euclidian worlds, worlds where locomotion does not behave exactly the same as VRC where people can stand on walls for instance, or more practically, large "vehicles" where everyone can be located on the vehicle which is "moving" through the world when the world is actually moving around it, but players outside the vehicle see the remote players attached to it properly.
This is all possible with how stations are currently synced, but it means that you need to have an object pool for every station in the world which is handled consistently between all clients, and it leaves stations subject to the worryingly common bugs with station sync. I have seen many people try using stations for locomotion and such only to stop because it's way more complex than it should be even though it's the way VRC tells you to do custom locomotion. There are also many worlds that you're leaving to use the jank method of pooling them which is liable to break, and on many of these worlds *has* broken when the station sync has broken. Despite it being more complex, people will make prefabs, people will make instructions for how to deal with station pooling
Because every VRC employee seems to be of the mindset of "man, should we support this basic thing that takes maybe a couple of hours to implement and should be basic to support?" I will reiterate: people already do these things, as time goes on, more people will do these things, you are increasing technical debt by *not* adding this. And it will only get worse the longer you do not act. When you run a content creation platform, lack of basic things like this pushes technical debt onto your creators, which means they use systems in ways they should not need to be used. This in turn means you need to support these further abstracted systems
Stations are the established and supported way to override VRC's built-in locomotion, and they should be able to be treated as such without hacking around to make them kinda work and leaving them subject to sync bugs.
Related bug about one of the ways station sync breaks currently:
https://feedback.vrchat.com/bug-reports/p/random-user-gets-stuck-in-station-for-new-joiners
title: Add option to mark VRCStation as local-only

Ideally we could use the Immobilze function in Udon with the following 4 options: 'Mobil' (or off), 'Translation', 'Rotation' and 'Both'. For desktop players that are currently using mouse and keyboard 'Rotation' should have no effect. If they used a controller on the other hand it should be active. Additionally maybe a bool option called 'AutoClearOnRespawn' or similar would be nice, although this could be done in Udon too...

1. Use a GameObject.get activeSelf node and a Boolean.UnaryNegation node with GameObject.SetActive to toggle the active state of some gameobject

In the first, the last value to be set ends up being the opposite truth value of the truth value just set by the GameObject.SetActive node one step earlier in the execution flow.
In the second image, the exact same value is referenced, but using a duplicate node, and the truth value matches the value set by the SetActive node as expected.
Note, this might be limited to references to properties of external GameObjects; when a simple boolean variable is substituted in for the active state of the GameObject, the graph executes as expected (see images three and four)

details:
World persistency would increase usability since old in-world settings could load automatically when the user re-visits the same world later. 
As worlds get more and more complex, this is no longer a "nice to have" feature - it is now absolutely needed to make a more complex world playable (such as playing a long story through like "The Devouring" for people who don't stay 4+ hours in a single world in VR or in case VRChat crashes while playing it). 
But it is also needed for grinding mechanics and worlds where you can build something and farm resources - something we are currently working on. 
Tl;dr, either VRChat gives us a [StoreToDisk] string datatype (without a weird character limit) that saves to disk when it changes and loads again when the user joins the same world or we'll have to implement our own open-source solution reading debug log files and a third-party application running on people's PCs to send Ctrl+V to the window handle (as other world creators have already done it).
But either way, we definitely can't go on without a solution here and the current "ask a VR user to copy+paste a string" is not a good way to do it - especially since it's not crash-safe, so users lose all progress when VRChat disconnects the user randomly. But also since we still don't have a "Copy to clipboard"/"Paste from clipboard" function next to a TextInput field for whatever reason, something that would be extremely useful for VR users in general anyway.
Ideally, an instance could also specify to only load the progress from whoever created it, since it's not possible right now to know who's the instance creator in Udon, but that's only a minor follow-up issue.
title: Save & Load persistent World Data

This canny requests to expose API such as:
- `ForceMeshUpdate`
- `UpdateGeometry`
- `maxDisplayedChars`
- `textInfo`

The text info is very important as it allows access to the `meshInfo` on each character mesh and the `vertices`.
The `meshInfo` exposes `mesh.vertices` and `vertices`, both are different and crucial.
title: Expose Methods on `TMProTextMeshPro`

details:
If you group up nodes in graphs it will noticeably reduce the response time of the graph.
Quickest way to reproduce: open up the Udon Graph "Projectile" (included in the SDK) and try adding a new variable. Note how long it takes for the variable to show up. Now select all the nodes in the graph and Remove from Group, then try adding a new variable again. It'll be noticeably faster. This can additionally be tested in the UdonSyncPlayer graph for a more extreme example of how much groups can slow things done.
Tested on SDK3 2021.02.23.11.40
title: Grouping nodes in Udon Graphs significantly impacts graph performance

details:
The open beta notification post suggests that SetOwner is instantaneous, but documentation suggests a request is sent to the current owner to confirm whether the ownership transfer is to be allowed.
If an ownership transfer request is to be approved by the current owner, this implies an extra two network round-trips will be added to the time before the new owner can begin syncing values. This overhead is crucial to account for in our designs.
Please document:
1. What is the ballpark expected latency between invoking SetOwner and having new values be serialized out? Does it depend on whether an OnOwnershipRequest event is defined?
2. What happens if you set variables in the time between calling SetOwner and when the OnOwnershipRequest is responded to by the current owner? Is there a possibility that they'll be overwritten by received values in that time?
These behaviors aren't currently defined in https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/udon-networking#object-ownership and have significant implications in complex networking designs.
title: Please precisely document latency costs of ownership transfers

-----
DESCRIPTION OF THE BUG (X):
Whenever a branched flow path is joined again, should the branch's bool have been "false", variables will be unaccessible and return NULL. Most functions, e.g. mathematical functions such as divisions, will also return NULL, even when both inputs are valid.
-----
DESCRIPTION OF THE BUG (Y):
Whenever a 2nd branch of a node references a variable that is referenced by another flow path, it will return NULL.
-----
STEPS TO REPRODUCE (how did you encounter the bug?): 
X: branch a flow path, join them back together, then return any variable. You should now have returned NULL when the lower branch path is taken. (returning a new const variable without any conversion will not cause this to happen).
Y: branch a flow path, and, in the lower path, reference (and work with) any variable node that is also referenced by the upper flow path. 
-----
IMAGES:
The Images below describe the refined code that causes these errors:
X (image with red letters):
When the boolean on the first branch (a) is true, everything works as intended. When it is false, the error occurs. 
The test outputs below, when a is false, demonstrate the following behaviour: b still prints the correct message (new const string, unchanged), c and d return NULL. iVelocity is a variable. Inserting int velocity or int number (e) from MidiNoteOn will also return NULL.
Y (Image without red letters):
Again, the branch bool being set to false and the lower path being taken, we see that the float (here 12.5) returns NULL after the toString. This does not occur if the upper debug.log is not connected to the toString node.
-----
RELATED POSTS AND BUG REPORTS:
After searching Canny and the forums, I could find the following related reports that can be related to the bugs:
1 - https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/reset-to-default-value-error (since not much information is posted here, this may be caused by the bug (X or Y) I described, especially since it appears "fairly random" to the author, just as it did to me at first.)
2 - https://ask.vrchat.com/t/why-your-time-get-time-node-is-probably-broken-and-how-to-avoid-it/2738 (While Time get Time is mentioned here, after testing, I can say that it does work, but that the error is caused by the bug I describe. You can see the author experiencing the bug Y on the lower Debug.Log node, having two Debug nodes accessing the same getTime node.)
3 - https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/erroneous-variable-behavior-with-chained-for-loops (similar issues appear on other "branching" nodes, every time the non-first pin is used)
4 - https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/subgraph-variables-cannot-be-referenced (Similar results to the bug (X or Y) in the old subgraph system. Maybe branches still use a system similar to the subgraph system, suggesting a fix by also implementing the SubProgram solution mentioned by Momo the Monster here?)
5 - https://ask.vrchat.com/t/jetdogs-tips-and-tricks/189/5 the statement "if you decide to use branches(if statements) you wont be able to link the next set of events." MAY have been incentivized by the error. Can not really be sure as not much information is given on why this statement is made.
-----
I am posting both bugs as one, as they are strikingly similar in nature and appear to be caused by the same problem. One fix here could potentially erase multiple bugs and solve multiple Canny posts, as shown above.
title: Branches decompose variables to NULL in certain scenarios

details:
When there is heavy transmit activity on a single frame, manually synced events can be dropped without retransmitting.
I've been unable to create a _minimal_ repro thus far, but I do have a consistent repro world for you at least: wrld_ca2bb56a-19c1-4ef5-8ef6-d060ae9fd8b0
Repro steps:
1. Connect two clients. In each, click the big vase next to the pens to enable world debugging options.
2. Click the shuffle button on either client and wait for shuffle to finish
3. Now, click the 'tile state histograms' button on the debug panel on both. The 'synced' values that appear should be the same (but, due to this bug, sometimes aren't). These directly measure the number of manually synced objects with a particular value for a synced state variable.
4. Click 'reveal tiles' on non-master to trigger another flurry of activity, then perform the histograms check on both again. The correct behaviour is for all of the synced variables to go to state 5, but in fact, on the master only about 100 change to 5, and the rest remain as they were.
Video of repro procedure: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fy3SG2qRTzo
This does not repro every time, but it seems to happen more than half the time for me. When it occurs, it seems that often, exactly 100 manually-synced objects are transmitted (and the rest remain unsynced until the next RequestSerialization), suggesting there might be an undocumented limit of some sort here.
If you're examining this in the editor, the objects in question are named "ManualSync" and each have a single synced int.
title: Manual syncs can be dropped during heavy network load

details:
It would be useful to be able to direct a VRCPlayerAPI to copy its voice locally to one or more specified audio sources. This would disable the network voice distance checks for the duration that the player api is directed at an audio source and force them to always send voice.
As https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/working-microphone-script has been closed I'm making a new canny in the Udon board since Phase said I should and I can't find a relevant one.
The player api voice settings are useful for many circumstances, but they lack control for if we want to relocate players voices. For instance if I wanted to make a walkie talkie, or an intercom system in a world, I'd need to settle for a unspatialized "voice of god." Even for stage performances where I want the voice to come from speakers in the world, it removes from the immersion to the point that I wouldn't really want to use the voice settings API.
A plus would be if this was implemented in a way that we could put stuff like high pass filters on the audio source and have them affect the voice that's mirrored to the audio source. This may involve a VRC-specific component to use as the target which goes on the same game object as the audio source.
It would also be nice to be able to send multiple player's voices to a single output. But not absolutely necessary since we could handle it if need be by having a different source for each player. If it were included, it'd be good to be able to control the volume of each player's input to the source.
title: Provide API to copy a player's voice to specified audio sources

details:
Since VRChat doesn't want modded clients but seems to do absolutely nothing to detect them and ban those users, we've seen a flood of Udon-related malicious mods recently which can mess around with the overall experience that map creators have been added through Udon. 
We can't expect every map creator to fully seal their creations against those clients, especially since the current system lacks any authentication of where a network event is coming from, making it way too easy for modded clients to abuse that system and most times impossible to secure the world against them. 
However, I've found out that it's extremely easy to detect some of those mods, and really don't understand why VRChat isn't doing the same. Do you want people to run around in worlds and ruin the fun for everyone? Have you ever tried staying in a public lobby without getting crashed by the same 5 people that do it every day?
Tl;dr, I'm willing to do it for you, please give me an API that I can use to self-report those users when my worlds detect one of their malicious mods. It's trivial to detect and even more easy to put booby traps everywhere which those hack0rs will fall into. 
Additionally, a world should also be able to self-disconnect a client on demand. And we need network events that pass a parameter of the player that sent the event, authenticated from the PUN server, not the sender itself. Ideally, we would also get an API that would allow us to use private/public keys to authenticate that a synced string has been set by the user that has the corresponding private key.
I'm aware that this is a neverending story and that there will be mods that can bypass this sooner or later, but we creators/users really just want to see that VRChat is doing at least some minimal effort against those malicious clients and are not letting them all get away with it. If there is some kind of fear that you actually ban users who run around messing with other people through malicious mods, they will reduce in numbers. It's usually not the "new user" that uses malicious mods, it's the "trusted user", which shows that there is nothing happening to ban them. Users speak openly about their mods and about crashing others in public lobbies as if they have absolutely nothing to fear, which unfortunately also seems to be the case as of now. I really hope this changes.
title: Add Self-Report API to Udon

Currently, the behavior when the bandwidth limit is exceeded seems to be that a single UdonBehaviour can queue up an arbitrary amount of data in the transmit queue. This can take tens of seconds to flush out, in some cases. This does not seem ideal; there's not a good way to detect when this is happening and back off to reduce bandwidth usage, so this could easily result in death runs where things get further and further behind.
I would suggest that, if a single UdonBehaviour has too many untransmitted serializations, then any RequestSerialization calls be deferred until the queue can be flushed.
You can reproduce the problem behaviour in this world: https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_cea2ef6d-13b3-439a-b876-539bb1691f57
Enter 4096 in one of the text boxes to start (attempted) transmitting way faster than the bandwidth limit. Let this run for a while, then set it back to 1. You'll see that (on the receive side) the received sequence numbers are well behind _instancewide_ for quite some time.
title: [Network Beta] Don't allow a single manually synced object to queue an arbitrary amount of untransmitted data

comments.body: Fixed in UnU Open Beta - build 1091. Reliable sync is now rate limited as a factor of the data size. The more you send, the more your rate is limited.

To expand on this a bit after seeing some confusion in discussions on discord about why this is needed - this fundamentally boils down to needing a way to help different UdonBehaviours and GameObjects to cooperate and share the limited bandwidth available in a fair manner.
In another Canny, there was a note that a getIsClogged will be added. This helps a bit, but it doesn't quite help enough. Consider if we have two UdonBehaviours that both want to send data. UdonBehaviour A checks getIsClogged, sees that it returns false, and proceeds to transmit. The network becomes clogged, and UdonBehaviour B sees that and refrains from transmitting. Later, the clog clears, but again UdonBehaviour A checks first, and transmits again (perhaps its timer for checking is shorter than B?). B never gets a chance to transmit. This is further complicated if there are multiple UBs on the same GameObject as well. This kind of pathological behavior can only be avoided with some kind of central control of when different GameObjects get a chance to transmit.
Explicitly setting a throttle in user code doesn't help either, because the network bandwidth cap is subject to change, the amount of bandwidth used by a sync operation is nontrivial to compute, and because if we set a throttle in a prefab for distribution, the value that throttle should have depends on what else is in the world and what it's doing at the time.
Finally, many prefab authors aren't going to be experts in network congestion control, and if you ask them to implement congestion control algorithms, they will get it wrong, guaranteed (but it'll probably work okay when they're testing in isolation!).
My proposal here is for a minimal change to help ensure that 1) UdonBehaviours share bandwidth in a fair manner, 2) latency doesn't get out of hand and 3) in most cases, prefab authors don't need to think about congestion control. This doesn't change existing semantics, because already RequestSerialization doesn't _immediately_ serialize, but waits a bit.
Simply making sure that Udon always waits for the queued data from a particular GameObject to finish sending before queueing up more ensures a more-or-less round-robin allocation of transmit opportunities among all GameObjects, limits the peak latency of transmission, and is probably what you want anyway for what is probably the majority of use cases where the final state of the synced vars is all that matters.

@{5de9405aea7cc52772fcc359|full_name}: I've done some testing on live. This does not yet seem to be resolved; after having one of my gameobjects sync really large arrays as fast as Udon will allow, other gameobjects still end up falling behind (and leaving the world hangs for a while as well). Repro steps are unchanged.

details:
Some manually synced objects are more critical to sync quickly than others - you might have some that need to sync a large amount of data (which might tie up a significant portion of the transmitter's bandwidth) but can do so slowly while others you'd like to respond immediately.
Currently, the bandwidth limit for manually synced objects seems to be instancewide, so if there's a single bandwidth hog it'll penalize everything. Having a way to set a QoS or priority value on a gameobject would allow the world author to select what suffers and degrade gracefully when bandwidth limits are exceeded; it would also greatly simplify bulk transmissions.
title: [Network Beta] Allow specifying QoS/priority of manually synced objects

details:
Specifically, I would like a clear point when I can know, for sure, that:
1. We know whether we are the instance master or not
2. RequestOwnership is expected to work normally
3. We can call GetOwner on any synced object (or at least the object receiving the event), and get someone who, if not the current owner, is at least a prior owner of that object.
4. We have observed player joins for what was, at one point after we started the join process, a complete list of players in the instance.
Currently this is a bit difficult; we can guess that, maybe after OnPlayerJoined or OnDeserialization things might be settled enough, but that might be later than necessary. If we're the first player we can only rely on OnPlayerJoined, but the first OnPlayerJoined is too early to have observed player joins for everyone who might be the owner of an object.
In particular, having a clear signal of whether we are the first master (and can freely set the initial state of objects) or whether we are expecting to deserialize object state would be very helpful.

details:
ORIGINAL BUG

Steps To Observe Behaviour:
1. Create two objects with VRC_ObjectSync components.
2. Add a VRC_Pickup script to one of the objects. 
3. Use the new networking debug menu that shows ownership, priority and data transfer per second to check the priority state of the two scripts.
Steps to Reproduce Bug:
1. Create an object with an ObjectSync script.
Expected Outcome:
You should be able to just mark an object sync object as Important without having to attach a dummy pickup script (and the associated dummy rigidbody)
Actual Outcome:
You're forced to add a pickup script to mark a sync object as high priority.

===

After Vowgan and I did more testing, we're getting less consistent results. I don't understand the logic for how something is Important - it seems like attaching a pickup script might help? Maybe if the syncer is enabled whilst it's in the player's view?

It'd be good to get some information on how Important/Normal priorities work and if the above (attaching a pickup script) actually makes a synced object higher priority as this is quite confusing at the moment.

===

Some more testing - it seems like ObjectSync is very inconsistent. Attaching a pickup has had the effect of actually totally desyncing the pos/rot of the ObjectSync'ed object in testing after doing a FlagDiscontinuity on the ObjectSync.

We're also seeing five-second lag on ObjectSync'ed objects in certain circumstances, generally again after firing FlagDiscontinuity on the ObjectSync.

(Apologies for this odd bug report - this is what happens when weird behaviour is observed *after* observing something in engine...)

===

We're using my pool test world to explore this behaviour: https://vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_7c23c9c3-fa6f-40ed-8f75-776fed2eef4e - I'll add some instructions for how to use the synced pickup system for QA to take a look at if they're interested.
title: [UNU v6] Strange ObjectSync behaviour observed during testing

details:
Allow world creators to choose where portals can and can't be dropped. This would help prevent "trolling" in public instances where someone might be forced into a portal against their will, some game worlds may have the player flying forward for example so they are unable to react fast enough or unable to act if a 2nd user places a portal in their path.
Right now the only options we have is entire world allows a portal or the entire world prevents portal dropping. A middle ground between these 2 extremes would be appreciated where a creator could have a designated area where portals can be dropped. Outside that and it would function the same as "too close to spawn".
As a world creator I don't want to remove the players choice of dropping portals but I would like some control over it to prevent unpleasant experiences for users visiting the world, as too many occurences like this can have a detrimental effect on public perception of a world.
title: World request: designating portal drop zones

details:
Issue:
When designing multiple worlds meant for navigation, IE an exploration based network of worlds that encourages groups of players to 'roam' between worlds, naturally exploring, it is currently extremely unreliable to expect players who all go through the same portal to actually end up in the same instance on the other end.
To compensate for this, world designers often opt to build larger monolithic worlds. This has negative consequences for the servers and players. If a player were to visit a world and only explore one quarter of it, they had to load and store 75% of the world unnecessarily, and the server had to consume those resources and bandwidth as well.
Proposal:
Some form of options on the portal object to be a new instance when spawned, inheriting the same privacy settings as the instance the portal was spawned in.
Effectively, when this is specified, upon the new instance containing the portals is generated, each of the portals also bind to a new instance. However, that of course would likely have disastrous effects, since you can create an infinite loop by just linking two worlds in a feedback loop together.
To solve this, two things probably are best to handle this.
1. The portal will lazy bind, only actually generating its instance the first time a user enters it
2. Portals should have some logic to detect if the world id they point to is the same as the world Id they were generated from. So if World A has a portal to World B, and World B has a portal to A, if I Go from A to B via instance generation, the B>A portal should use the instance it "came from" rather than generating a new one.
The intended effect here would be such that if a user hops through a portal to a new instance, then returns back via a "return" portal that world happens to have setup, they can semi reliably expect to end up back in the instance they came from with their friends again.
(Caveats of course for if this would involve them trying to join an already full instance, in which case it would overflow them to a new instance as a fallthrough)

If there is an intention specifically to encourage meeting of strangers behind the current design, then there is potentially one more caveat to add to the portal's instance selection, and that would be a "Fit First" sorting to instance selection.

This would effectively prioritize, rather than spinning up a new instance, instead selecting a "everyone can fit" instance if possible. For example, if World A has 8 users in it and a portal to World B, which has a max capacity of 24 users, the portal would first attempt to find a currently existing instance that *also* has room for all 8 users to fit into, and prioritize that zone first.

Reason:
A fair number of world builders, myself included, are really seeming to dig more into the artistic and design style of building individual worlds that cohesively "glue" together to encourage and reward players for taking portals and exploring, which I believe is a core design philosophy of the VRC team.
However, player's suspension of disbelief and engagement becomes interrupted often when they attempt to travel between worlds and often find their group of friends becomes broken up and scattered across different instances.
This "downside" encourages world designers to instead opt into more monolithic, larger style worlds that manually handle exploration/trave/teleportation within the world itself.
Unfortunately, these large monolithic worlds are quite the burden, if not incompatible, with quest users, which appears to be an important demographic for the VRC team.
In order to encourage world designers to "break up" their worlds into managable sizes (which lowers hardware requirements and encourages lazy loading of unused assets not explored), it is imperative a more cohesive logic be baked into how portals between worlds works.
Summary
If we make portals less random feeling and more consistent between worlds, it will encourage world makers to make more smaller worlds, rather than unified monolithic worlds, which is better for Quest users for sure, and probably just better for server health/bandwidth overall.
title: Add support for "New Instance" synched to first enter on Portals

Currently network IDs for objects are determined based on their position in the hierarchy. This makes it difficult to make PC/Quest cross-compatible worlds (eg, you can't just EditorOnly out a whole tree of PC-specific stuff), and makes it so the smallest changes to a world break instances with mixed versions.
