title: [Udon Networking] Set network ID based on metadata attached to game objects

details:
One serious issue with main-thread heavy processes is that heavy mathematical calculations sitting on that thread can seriously slow down the runtime.
Udon especially has this problem due to the high CPU load of even individual mathematical operations compared to native Unity C#.
A proposal to help with this would be to draw on the Node developers' solution to this same problem. Node, like normal JS, is based on a single thread that is designed to interact with the DOM. However, the Node developers recognized that a worker thread system would allow them to pull heavy mathematics jobs onto different threads.
This model seems like it would be interesting to explore with Udon. Some reading is below:
https://nodejs.org/api/worker_threads.html
https://livecodestream.dev/post/how-to-work-with-worker-threads-in-nodejs/
https://nodesource.com/blog/worker-threads-nodejs/
title: Add Node.js style "Worker Threads" to offload CPU-heavy mathematics etc. to

details:
# Problem
If an Animator and an UdonBehaviour are components of the same GameObject, the Root Motion setting in the animator is disabled.
# Why it's a problem
Root Motion is normally **enabled** by default on Animators. Adding an UdonBehaviour can unexpectedly break animators.
# Workarounds
- Don't put Animators and UdonBehaviours onto the same object if you want to use root motion. (However, this prevents us from using Animation Events!)
- Use the following U# code proposed by CyanLaser
```
OnAnimatorMove() {
     animator.ApplyDefaultRootMotion();
}
```
# Proposed fix
Add a toggle to UdonBehaviours which lets us directly control the root motion setting.
# Related
https://ask.vrchat.com/t/fix-for-animator-apply-root-motion-position-and-rotation/296
title: UdonBehaviours disable Root Motion on Animators

details:
When reading a variable in Udon, the visible execution flow does not pass through the node. All that is known is that the read occurs some time before its value is used.
However, when the variable in question is set earlier in the execution flow[within the same event], it is not clear from the graph whether or not the read occurs before or after the set.
However, it gets even worse when the output of the same variable read node is used both before and after the set in the graph[on the same event execution flow].
Is the read performed again after the set(effectively splitting a variable read node into two nodes), or is the output from before the set held on the stack?

My proposed solution is adding a variable get node that does pass through the visible execution flow, to specifically define when the read occurs(the existing variable get nodes' behaviour wouldn't be changed)

See the attached images for example graph snippets where the order of reads can change results but isn't apparent from the graph.
title: Order of variable reads unclear.

details:
At the moment, making a player locally disappear from view for you requires messing with VRC Stations in a way that they were not really intended to be messed with.
There's a few good reasons why a Udon toggle for being able to make a player totally disappear would be a good idea:
1. In game worlds, allow for 1 player sections, like cutscenes or tutorials.
2. In private events, allow for vetting of a guest before they show up to anyone outside of a whitelist.
3. In large maps, allow for area load/unload within the high-precision space near origin without seeing another player walking around on a different bit of the map.
4. Performance - allowing a large number of people in a map but allowing players to limit the load somewhat if they have a weaker PC.
Note that much of this is already possible with hacky implementations using stations. A visibility toggle just makes this easier.
title: Add a hide/show toggle into VRCPlayerApi

It would be beneficial to users to provide a lightweight option to spawn a specific object using the VRCObjectPool component. This would make it easier for new and experienced World Creators to spawn specific objects, in a simple manner, without having to rely on complex systems to manually synchronize the active states of objects.

details:
TeleportTo instantly moves a player to a position. 
Normally it makes sense that this would send an RPC in order to update the player's position as fast as possible for other players.
The "lerpOnRemote" option for this function should omit the RPC and rely on VRChat's regular player-position sync.
However, this isn't the case and seems to send unnecessary RPC's.
This function COULD be useful for things such as moving platforms, but due to this oversight repeated calls will result in "unexpected client behaviour" and a disconnect.
title: TeleportTo sending unnecessary RPC's when LerpOnRemote is enabled

details:
Ever since this "Udon Network Update" There's been a VERY common bug where oftentimes, if a player joins a lobby, nobody that's already in the lobby will see, nor hear said player- essentially making them a ghost.
For me, I'll get this bug about 1 in 4 lobbies I join. Whether it's public, friends+, invite, whatever- I'll join a world fine on my end and literally nobody can see nor hear me. Often times I'll only know I have the bug if people are stepping in front of me or are completely ignorant of what I do. It's only after I reconnect that people will say "Oh where were you," after telling them I was trying to talk to them for the past 10 minutes.
When this incredibly annoying bug occurs, I'll have to either rejoin the instance- or block and unblock all the people already present in the world- those of who cannot see me.
There's even been times where I thought I had the bug (but didn't), rejoined the instance, then for real, actually got the bug when I reconnected.
And this isn't some per-person bug or anything. Word about this is going around everywhere. As for my own troubleshooting, changing the status of my firewall, restarting my router, changing router settings, network settings, network speeds, launching as administrator, etc., nothing that I can do from my end prevents this atrocious bug from occurring.
For example: I played VRChat last night and I joined a total of about 8 lobbies. In literally 3 out of those 8 lobbies I joined, nobody could see me. This is incredibly infuriating as I'll try to talk to my friends and chime into conversations, and they completely ignore me as I'm apparently not there for anybody who's already in the instance.
I'm not meaning to complain about the Udon Network Update, as I know there's a lot of intrepid creators taking advantage of its new syncing parameters and new netcode. But oh my God, this is the worst game-breaking update-bug that I've seen in 3 whole years. It almost makes VRChat unplayable.
If I can't "chat" in "VRChat" in 3 out of 8 lobbies, this is more than just a problem. Please fix this, and please soon.
title: Udon Network Update (UnU) Severely Broke Player Presence/Player Sync in Rooms/Lobbies/Worlds

details:
When calling RequestSerialization(), we expect that OnPreSerialization() / OnPostSerialization() is called afterwards from VRChat. This doesn't happen however when we are alone in an instance, since no data is sent over network then, even after calling RequestSerialization(). 
This makes networking logic more complicated then it needs to be. 
It would be better if VRChat would check if playercount is 1 and directly call OnPreSerialization() / OnPostSerialization() with result.success when RequestSerialization() is being called, even when no data is serialized in reality.
title: Also call OnPreSerialization() / OnPostSerialization() when being alone in an instance

details:
I would love to create a matchmaking/game hub world, where users can meet up with each other. It would be great if there was a way, using Udon, to drop a portal to a specified world ID, with the specified instance type, at a specified position and rotation.
I suppose it would be just like dropping a portal manually-- it simply does not get created if it's in an invalid position (too close to spawn or another player).
Why not just drop a portal using the menu? Because it would be a nice shortcut to integrate it into the world somehow, like with a button or animation.
Why not just use a normal portal? Those put you in public instances, and I would love to have the same target instance consistency as dropping an invite-only portal manually.
title: Udon method to drop an invite+/invite only portal

details:
I'm working on drivable cars with Udon and I've added full support for game controllers like steering wheel setups and gamepads, but I've hit a roadblock with the steering input axis due to the 10-20% dead zone that is meant for thumb sticks.
With the current configuration I'm clearing all input fields for Joy1 Axis [1-10] and then using Joy2 Axis [1-4] for throttle, brake, clutch and steering.
Everything else works fine, including the H-shifter with 6 gears and reverse, but steering is simply unusable when you have to turn the wheel 90 degrees to see any kind of response in game.
It would be really helpful to have official support for dead zone free input so 3rd party applications aren't necessary to middle man the inputs using MIDI (or OSC is the future)
My wild guess for a potential solution would be to add additional virtual input axes with no dead zone on top of the existing ones.

Video: https://twitter.com/Varneon/status/1406703700987551749
title: Add a way to get game controller input axis values without dead zone

details:
MonoBehaviour.OnRenderObject() gets called on every frame on every script in the scene that has it declared.
UdonBehaviour having every Unity event declared causes OnRenderObject() to be called on every UdonBehaviour in the world even if they don't have anything in them, which can quickly add up to a significant increase in frametime.
With 10000 empty UdonBehaviours in the scene I ended up with the following results:
	1) Unity Editor: ≈4.2ms (≈240 FPS)
	2) VRChat: ≈14.7ms (≈70 FPS)
Here are 2 more worlds in VRChat as a point of reference:
	1) Empty plane: ≈2.4ms (≈410 FPS)
	2) 1000 empty UdonBehaviours: ≈5.2ms (≈190 FPS)
I have attached an image of the Unity Editor deep profiler timeline showing that OnRenderObject() gets called on the UdonBehaviours at the end of the frame
Also in case of any misunderstanding about the meaning of "OnRenderObject" I want to state that it has nothing to do with having a renderer component attached to the same object - "OnRenderObject is called after camera has rendered the Scene"
Unity also clearly states the following in their documentation: "Be aware that this function can have a performance impact because it runs on for every GameObject with a script that uses this callback."
https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/MonoBehaviour.OnRenderObject.html
title: UdonBehaviour.OnRenderObject() causes inevitable unnecessary static overhead

comments.body: Fixed in 2021.3.1

details:
While attempting to build a multiplayer arcade cabinet, I ran into a somewhat unintuitive behaviour. 
Setting Ownership to another player in the same tick as updating a synced variable and requesting serialization causes a race. Sometimes the targeted player receives ownership *before* the latest synced variables. Other times they receive it *after* the latest Synced variables. This means that logic can be unpredictable / inconsistent, as the normally garaunteed manual sync becomes, well, less garaunteed. 
I am not sure if it is the intended behaviour, but if it is it should probably be spelled out in the docs at least (responding to or closing this would serve as documentation too! :) )
In the end I was able to work around the race condition by sending a playerId along with the rest of the synced data and using that in the OnDeserialized hook to set ownership with a garauntee of having the latest data, but this seems convoluted and unintuitive, so I'd prefer to see it patched so other folks don't spend a few hours pulling hair out.
Either way, thanks for your time! <3
title: Setting Ownership to someone else in the same tick as RequestSerialization causes a race condition

details:
Right now we can only do `SendCustomEvent` via an animation file while the animator is on the same gameObject as a UdonBehaviour. There are various ways to do this within a state, but it will still require a animation file.
However, if we had a StateMachineBehaviour for SendCustomEvent (and Set Variable) we could do this without needing extra animators, and potentially not have the requirement of needing a UdonBehaviour on the same gameObject as the animator. Possibly reducing the overall UdonBehaviours in a scene depending on the creators need.
Whether or not it will support all the state machine behaviour methods will be a design/performance choice.
https://docs.unity3d.com/540/Documentation/ScriptReference/StateMachineBehaviour.html
SendCustomEvent
- State Method (OnStateEnter/OnStateExit/OnStateIK/OnStateMove)
- UdonBehaviour
- value
Set Variable
- State Method (OnStateEnter/OnStateExit/OnStateIK/OnStateMove)
- UdonBehaviour
- name
- value
Alternative
- State Method (OnStateEnter/OnStateExit/OnStateIK/OnStateMove)
- UdonBehaviour
- Type (Send Event / Set Variable)
- Name? (Set Variable)
- Value
These are just examples, and will not reflect on how or if VRC will implement it.
title: SendCustomEvent/Set Variable StateMachineBehaviour for animators

details:
With the recent addition of the OnVariableChange event, UdonGraph users can now react to when the variable is updated. If the variable with a change callback has an initial value that is not the default for that type, the old value is incorrect for the first call of the change event. 
VRChat build 1114
VRCSDK3 2021.07.13.13.39
See screenshot for example graph. It defines a bool variable with the default value to true. On Interact flips its value. The change callback will then set the enabled state of two gameobjects. The first call will always disable both objects as _old_value is initialized to false instead of true.
title: OnVariableChange old value has incorrect initial value

details:
When using the OnVariableChange call back for variables, synced variable changes and SetProgramVariable() both will update the variable and call the callback. These methods will also update the old value saved, but only before calling the callback and not after. The old value is left in a bad state. This means that a combination of SetProgramVariable/OnDeserialization followed with changing the value directly in Graph (or CyanTriggers) will not have the proper old value during the change callback.
Note, this affects both UdonGraph and CyanTriggers.
VRChat build 1114
VRCSDK3 2021.07.13.13.39
See screenshot for example graph. The graph contains an interact to change the variable directly, a "Toggle" event to change the variable using SetProgramVariable, and an OnVariableChange event to react to either. If you call the "Toggle" event and then call the "Interact" event, the OnVariableChange event will have both value and oldValue equal to the same data.
title: OnVariableChange old value not updated with SetProgramVariable or synced variable changes

comments.body: Closing after conversation with CyanLaser on how this is handled in the GraphCompiler.

After discussing with Merlin, it is suggested that the compilers should be handling setting of the old value at the end of the change callback. This means that this canny is more a bug for the UdonGraph compiler and not the runtime handling of when the change callback is called from SetHeapVariable.
From my point of view, it is still unclear on vrchat's intentions if runtime should handle this or the compiler. It would be nice if there was better documentation on handling these events for compiler writers. Since writing this canny I have updated CyanTriggers to set the value at the end of the change callback.

comments.body: I visited the world and I see this. Could you tell me more about what you expect to happen?
@{5de9405aea7cc52772fcc359|full_name}: I expect for the video to stall playing until the point it is assigned is loaded.

@{5de9405aea7cc52772fcc359|full_name}: I expect it to work as it did in AVPro 2.0.7 where when you seek to a point in the media, it would immediately skip to that point and start loading the buffer from that timestamp onward, not just jump to the nearest loaded data.

For example, if you are watching a movie with some close friends, and another friend joins like an hour in, that late joiner should be able to skip to the timestamp that the others are at, which is how it worked in 2.0.7.

@{5de9405aea7cc52772fcc359|full_name}: I made a video showing it in my test world here. 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CO3EEc2Wlp0
First video loaded is just a youtube video that's just a playlist of audio so the file size is small, buffer happens quite fast, and it's reflected as such when jumping through the video. When I load an actual video, the buffer doesn't load as much and takes longer, and is also reflected as such. It had worked prior to the new AVPro version. I'm surprised this isn't as big an issue for people. Do people just not use AVPro or something? It basically breaks all ability to set the video time which makes it way too risky to watch any videos of substantial length with AVPro because if any late joiners need to come in they can't sync up.
Edit - And just went to a random movie world since mine is busted that seemed to work and I didn't realize it used AVPro. Someone crashed and when they tried to join we tried to sync them up by reloading the video. Once we reloaded I observed the exact same behavior/buffer issue.

@{5de9405aea7cc52772fcc359|full_name}: 
To further test this issue, I grabbed the trial 2.1.6 version, used YTDL to get a raw link and used their media player example scene to test skipping the buffer point.
Here's the recording: https://streamable.com/k6eube
It appears to work 100% fine with raw AVPro, but when trying to skip forward within VRChat, it still only moves to the end of the current available video buffer instead of skipping and resume loading from the new selected timestamp.

In addition to this, I was reminded that the AVPro upgrade from 2.0.7 to 2.1.5 happened on the same update as then auto-resync logic addition. https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/vrchat-202131
I have suspicions that this could be connected to this buffer bug.
Also I realize that I tested on 2.1.6 before but that VRChat is currently on 2.1.5. I have just tested 2.1.5 as well and got the same result of it working as expected.
@{5de9405aea7cc52772fcc359|full_name}: Necroing to say this is no longer the case and the issue can be closed.
@{5f6be62b15f9fa5364f1834c|full_name}: Thanks, we'll take another look on our end and close it out if we can confirm!

details:

details: World developers seeking to create complex worlds that handle arrays could greatly improve their development process if they were able to use Generic Collections, especially List<T>. There are many common situations where Collections and LINQ combined can reduce large quantities of code to simple one-line or one-operation solutions.
title: Expose C# Generic Collections (List<T>, Dictionary<TKey,TValue>, etc.)

details:
By default, a user can always grab a pickup with the other hand while holding it with one hand, to switch hands. 
This becomes a problem e.g. when you create a controller that needs to be held in one hand and operated with the other hand, sudden unwanted hand switches can occur, you cannot make the user press "grab" with the other hand in reach of that pickup. This also becomes a problem e.g. if you want to track something while the pickup is held, because the OnDrop+OnPickup event will fire while still holding it, even though it was never dropped.
We need the ability to disable hand switching on a pickup without dropping the pickup first. 
Unfortunately, disabling the "pickupable" property in OnPickup does not already enable this behavior. I would at least expect that doing that leads to the wanted result of disallowing a hand switch.
title: Disallowing Pickup Hand Switch

details:
It was only a matter of time until an exploit would break every Udon-based user authentication system over night, but here we are.
Affected is:
- every Udon moderation tool
- every Udon whitelisting tool
- every Patreon enhancement system
- every access control system for private worlds that should stay private until they are released, but need to have public test user sessions
The situation right now: People go in worlds, gain access that they should not have, and ruin other people's fun by pretending to be the world author.
Here is my proposed solution which would allow us to "fix" this:
1. Private user certificates
- every user needs a private certificate in their client, which can be used to encrypt or sign a synced string in a function like EncryptString(string input) which returns the string encrypted with that local private certificate.
2. Public user certificates
- every user needs access to the public certificates of other users to be able to decript a string in a function like DecryptString(string encryptedStr, string userID)
- the userID needs to be the one from the VRChat website, or alternatively the display name (please don't), only having the public certificate from others in your current instance would not be enough
The goal of this is to allow a safe user-to-user communication in which you can trust that whatever arrives on your side from the network to really be from that specific user, and that a user who pretends to be user X is able to decrypt a secret string which was encrypted by that user's certificate once. On top of that, authenticating a network-event (knowing where it came from) would also allow additional security.
title: We need User Certificates ASAP

details:
Create a way to make Udon Behaviours executed server-side (by putting the server as the default owner of objects for instance).
This would allow more stability for multiplayer games. It could reduce by twice the latency and solve the problems when the master goes afk or crashes.
Moreover, it would simplify a lot the process of transferring the ownership while a game is running and the master leaves or crashes for example.
title: Make Udon execute serverside

details:
When using sendChange on a synced variable, the owner and remote clients will have inconsistent results when the variables remains the same:
The owner will activate the Change event for that variable every time regardless if the variable was actually changed, whereas remote clients will only activate the Change event if the variable has actually changed.
Attached is a picture of an example graph for testing the problem, where every 2 seconds the SyncedInt is changed to the number 7. The results will be that the owner will print 7 to the log every 2 seconds, but remote clients will only print it once (because the value is changed from 0 to 7 initially)
title: [SDK 2021.07.13.13.39] Variable Change event inconsistent between owner and remote when the variable is not actually changed

details:
If you sync a vrcurl or an array, their respective variable Change events will activate every time there's a deserialization for non-owners. This will happen regardless of if sendChange is on or not, they will be considered Changed every time.
The attached picture is an example graph: Even though the SyncedInt is the only variable being changed, the SyncedURL and SyncedIntArray Change events will also activate for non-owners.
title: [SDK 2021.07.13.13.39] Synced vrcurl and arrays activate Change events for non owners on every deserialization

**UdonBehaviour.cs original code**

```
1069:            foreach ((string symbolName, object _) in programVariables)
1070:            {
1071:                SetProgramVariable(symbolName, null);
1072:            }
```

```
1069:            foreach ((string symbolName, object _) in programVariables)
1070:            {
1071:                if (!_symbolNameCache.TryGetValue((eventName, symbolName), out string newSymbolName))
1072:                {
```

details:
VRChat introduced graphics settings in the beta client now, which modifies the LOD bias, resulting in LOD0 not being active when it should.
This is breaking some scripts in our world, because the Update() loop checks for LOD0 being rendered to know that the player is close and the object is in sight before running code.
Toggling script logic via LOD renderer (specifically LOD0) is a common way how optimization in UDON is done right now, which is also from the official Unity tutorial https://learn.unity.com/tutorial/fixing-performance-problems
VRChat cannot argue that we should use area toggles everywhere instead, since those still have their own issues which makes them unusable in some cases https://vrchat.canny.io/bug-reports/p/colliders-that-are-not-on-the-mirrorreflection-layer-will-stop-the-hand-raycasts
To solve this, we should be able to define our own graphics settings overrides, which would solve the LOD bias issue that we now need to account for. At least the LOD bias should be optionally defineable for a world.
title: Some graphics settings break LOD renderer script logic

details:
Currently, OnTriggerEnter and friends will trigger collisions for some protected objects - notably, colliders on avatars, but there may be others as well. This is a common point of confusion as your UdonBehaviour may suddenly die when it tries to examine a collider, and you may have difficulty reproducing this (because your avatar doesn't have colliders or triggers on it).
I suspect it's rare to actually need this functionality; while there may be specific use cases that need to detect colliders on avatars, or maybe the quick menu, but for the most part it's just a debugging rabbit hole for Udon beginners. As such, I suggest that Udon filter these events, and guarantee that OnTriggerEnter and friends only be invoked when the collider is not a protected object.
It may be necessary for compatibility to add a flag to retain the old behavior - but the presence of protected colliders is in any case subject to change as VRC's UI changes, or as a player changes avatars, and they can still be potentially found by performing sphere/raycasts, so there are workarounds available for weird usecases.
title: OnTrigger/Collider Enter/Stay/Exit should not fire for protected objects (at least, not by default)

details:
Currently, most assets built with non-graph compilers (i.e. U#) require that the compiler be present, and inject a bunch of C# into your project. This is both a security risk (because you're pulling in editor extensions which can do whatever they like) and a usability issue (you need to pull in a rather large asset, and even if you do want to use U#, your compilation times keep growing as you add assets).
It would be nice to be able to compile this U# code and distribute just the compiled asset. This is _almost_ possible today, but needs a bit more support to be possible without the need for editor scripting to load the compiled code.
In particular, what is needed is a subtype of UdonProgramAsset, distributed as part of the VRCSDK, which:
1. Serializes the program within the ProgramAsset (the current UdonProgramAsset does not do this, and needs to be subclassed to be usable)
2. Hides the default disassembly view in the inspector
3. Provides a public function to set the contents based on an IUdonProgram, or a SerializedUdonProgramAsset.
Today, if you wanted to do this precompiled asset distribution, you'd still need your own subclass of UdonProgramAsset that extracts the serialized program from the source SerializedUdonProgramAsset and shoves it into its own fields, and then loads it back later; editor extensions aren't quite avoidable today.
title: Please provide a way to distribute compiled Udon code

details:
In some cases, a prefab containing an UdonBehaviour can end up with a null serializedProgramAsset, even though the referenced UdonProgramSource has a serialized program asset associated with it. This then results in a failure to load the program:

```
[<color=yellow>UdonBehaviour</color>] Could not load the program; the UdonBehaviour on 'SpherePrefab(Clone)' will not run.
UnityEngine.Debug:Log (object,UnityEngine.Object)
VRC.Core.Logger:Log (string,int,UnityEngine.Object)
VRC.Udon.UdonBehaviour:InitializeUdonContent () (at Assets/Udon/UdonBehaviour.cs:1143)
VRC.Udon.UdonManager:RegisterUdonBehaviour (VRC.Udon.UdonBehaviour) (at Assets/Udon/UdonManager.cs:668)
VRC.Udon.Wrapper.Modules.ExternVRCInstantiate:__Instantiate__UnityEngineGameObject__UnityEngineGameObject (VRC.Udon.Common.Interfaces.IUdonHeap,uint[]) (at Assets/Udon/WrapperModules/ExternVRCInstantiate.cs:69)
VRC.Udon.VM.UdonVM:Interpret ()
VRC.Udon.UdonBehaviour:RunProgram (uint) (at Assets/Udon/UdonBehaviour.cs:884)
VRC.Udon.UdonBehaviour:RunEvent (string,System.ValueTuple`2<string, object>[]) (at Assets/Udon/UdonBehaviour.cs:1066)
VRC.Udon.UdonBehaviour:ManagedUpdate () (at Assets/Udon/UdonBehaviour.cs:447)
VRC.Udon.UdonManager:Update () (at Assets/Udon/UdonManager.cs:251)
```

This issue has cropped up a few times in the wild, and with the help of Haï~ I have a minimal repro procedure (using only Udon Graph, to make sure it's not an U# bug):

1. Create a new project and import VRCSDK3-WORLD-2021.08.11.15.16_Public
2. Import this unitypackage: https://www.dropbox.com/s/572efzuno9xvbbm/fails%20to%20set%20serialized%20program%20source.unitypackage?dl=0
3. Initially, if you enter play mode, you will see two spheres, which both turn green. One is a spawned prefab, one is a prefab instance present from scene load.
4. Delete the SerializedUdonPrograms folder.
5. Enter play mode again. You'll see two spheres, but only one will turn green; the spawned prefab will fail to load its udon program with the stacktrace above.

Once in this state, editing or recompiling the udon program does not fix it; however, it can be fixed by opening and closing the prefab.
I'm pretty sure there are other ways to enter this state than deleting the SerializedUdonPrograms directory, but this is the only consistent repro procedure we've found so far.
title: UdonBehaviours on Prefabs don't set their serializedProgramAsset, resulting in program load failures

details:
Looping over all childs of a transform to find a certain child with a given name is really expensive in Udon. It's what takes one of the biggest performance hits currently in our scripts. You cannot use Transform.Find() in a lot of cases which is the closest Unity function to that.
I noticed that having a native function from VRChat doing this for us would be a good way to increase performance, especially if this search is also done over childs of childs etc., while it's also easily to implement.
Ideally, we would get a GetChildWithName() function that returns the child which has a name that starts with a given string (so instead of String.Equals it uses String.StartsWith()), plus the optional parameter if disabled gameObjects should be included or not, and an optional parameter if this search should only be performed for direct childs or also for childs of childs (all layers down). Furthermore, a function that returns an array of all findings would be great. These functions could be added to the Utilities class for example. 
Note: Transform.Find(), which is the closest Unity function to this, does not perform a recursive descend down a Transform hierarchy, so it does not cover this use case.
title: Please give us a GetChildWithName() function with additional parameters

details:
We need to know in Udon if someone is using SDK2 or SKD3 avatars and also if they use FBT, e.g. to give them a station which doesn't break their avatar, or to not let them into a specific station and display a message instead. 
Right now, we can either make a station that fully works for SDK3 avatars or for SDK2 avatars. When it comes to FBT users, it get's even more complicated for certain use cases. There are also things that should work differently if the user has full body tracking, not related to stations at all.
"But what are you doing that breaks SDK2/3 avatars?"
We e.g. import parts of the Avatar SDK3 into our SDK3 world unity project to override certain tracking by animation and to adjust the viewpoint. We do this because else the animation / viewpoint only works for SDK2 avatars. Using those components breaks SDK2 avatars. It also breaks some stuff on SDK3 when they exit, like finger tracking, or IK, but the user can at least manually reset their avatar to fix that.
"But wouldn't it be better to fix stations instead?"
We are waiting for working stations since forever and a fix for them usually breaks with the next update. There are so many broken/unexpected behaviour things with stations that we should not wait until an update will fix all issues we are having on our weird use-cases. A lot of people do awesome stuff by using stations in unintended ways or want to tailor something to be used by FBT or a certain avatar version, not only limited to stations.
Note: There is a guide regarding stations where the avatar version can branch in an animator. This is good, but does not cover any use case, especially if you need the information without or before having the user in a station. https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/vrc_station#sdk3-station-with-sdk2sdk3-avatar
title: Request: Get Avatar SDK Version and FBT bool from VRCPlayerApi

details:
According to a response from Phasedragon on the official discord, putting a UdonBehaviour with None syncmode on a gameobject will break syncing for any other UBs on that gameobject.
When building reusable components, it would be preferable to be able to slap None mode onto any UdonBehaviour that does not, itself, require sync, while still being able to add other UdonBehaviours that need sync. Consider, for example, a simple UdonBehaviour that adds collision sounds to any rigidbody. We should be able to add this regardless of whether the object is synced or not. With the proposed None sync mode behavior, it would be necessary to mark this helper UB as being either continuous or manual sync mode (and it would only be able to coexist with UB of the same type).
If, instead, none sync mode was considered 'weaker' than ObjectSync, Continuous, or Manual modes, and to defer to those modes if a corresponding component was present, we'd have much better composability than the proposed semantics.
title: SyncMode None should be "weaker" than other sync modes

Currently in Udon that array is out of order for different clients, and individual playerIds represent their join order, rather than an autofilled sequence from players leaving and joining.

It would also be useful for sorting VRCPlayerApis by a world's game score for a scoreboard.  Array.Sort is extremely useful because, even though we don't have access to custom data structures or IComparable implementations in Udon, we can still sort things using associated arrays of intrinsic data types.

And before you do the same thing that you did with the previous post, please just whitelist everything you can.  Not just Array methods.  Stringbuilders.  Native Unity components like LODGroups.  Although a rumor, I heard that ReflectionProbe endpoints weren't included for a YEAR after Udon's release because there was a blacklist for anything with 'reflection' in the name.  Please consider going back through the whitelist and enabled anything and everything possible.

StaticBatchingUtility.Combine sets up static batching for several objects at runtime. It offers the following advantages over marking objects as batching static in the editor:
-Allows the performance advantages of static batching to be applied to objects generated at runtime. Since such objects don't exist in the editor, it's not possible to mark them as batching static. 
-Objects setup to be statically batched in this way can be moved by adjusting the transform of their associated staticBatchingRoot gameobject. This is useful for sets of objects that move together as a whole.
For these reasons exposing StaticBatchingUtility.Combine would provide world creators with a useful tool for optimizing their worlds.
https://docs.unity3d.com/2019.4/Documentation/ScriptReference/StaticBatchingUtility.html

details:
Please expose layout based key checks so creators can provide better user experience in worlds.
Unity's input system has methods for checking keyboard keys based on the location of the keyboard rather than the specific letter. VRChat has a global player base which means users can have any possible keyboard layout. Most world creators assume the user will have the qwerty keyboard layout, but any other layout may cause issues with the selected input key checks. World creators currently have no way to resolve this. 
As an example, the French keyboard layout swaps the A and Q keys from the qwerty layout. This means that using the Q key would always fire when the user tries to move left. The Q key is near the wasd movement keys and seems like a good option, but creates a bad experience for users using the French keyboard layout.
title: Expose Keyboard location based input keys

details:
Previously exposed TMP methods are not exposed any longer (or maybe never really were).
For instance, `ForceMeshUpdate` was exposed in update 2021.4.1 (https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/vrchat-202141)
for both `TextMeshPro` and `TextMeshProUGUI` but is *unavailable* for `TextMeshPro`.
Note the difference that `TextMeshProUGUI` is for canvases and `TextMeshPro` for being placed inside the scene.

This was talked about a bit in #udon-questions
Rather than exposing a Player Transform directly (which can lead to security issues)
I purpose a wrapped class that stores the reference to the Transform (but doesn't expose it) and only exposes the non-destructive parts of Transform to the end user.
Essentially TrackingData except extended to allow for more than just Head and Hands and allows usage of methods such as TransformPoint, InverseTransformPoint, TransformDirection, etc.
Wrapper methods within the wrapped class could be restricted for security purposes and developers could use Transform methods in a secure manner right off the wrapped class instance.
The main difference between this and what Udon does now is being able to access methods that are otherwise not exposed and the VRChat developers still being able to maintain security over those exposed methods.
For example lets call our wrapped class WrappedTransform.
The instance of WrappedTransform wouldn't be passible to Object.Destroy but a world developer could still use something like WrappedTransform.InverseTransformPoint if they wanted.
title: Expose a Wrapped Class for Restricted Object Transforms

details:
Whilst the addition of Copy/Paste to the keyboard is welcome in [1220], there may be times when a world developer wishes to initiate a copy for text data via udon.
 —
# Examples
1. A world developer has user persistent data. They wish for the user to save this user persistent data without potential for error, such as deletion of text using the on-screen keyboard. As such, they provide a "Copy" button, that when pressed, writes to the clipboard, allowing the user to paste the data elsewhere for storage.
2. A user has a video player. However, they wish to improve Quest compatibility by providing a "URL converter" that takes popular media links and converts them to a link-resolver equivalent, as is common. Rather than risk the user accidentally back-spacing portions of the URL which they cannot see within the VRCHAT keyboard, they intelligently convert and copy the new URL `on End Edit`, for the user to paste into a video player address bar.
3. A world developer is hosting an event. During this event, they wish to provide codes which are linked to a website for various event-related activities or interactions. Rather than force the user to exit VRChat unnecessarily by way of URL, they provide a menu in-world to copy the code(s) at any time, which can be pasted into a website at a later time.
 —
# Request
Please add support for the [GUIUtility.systemCopyBuffer](https://docs.unity3d.com/2019.4/Documentation/ScriptReference/GUIUtility-systemCopyBuffer.html), by adding a `GUIUtility set systemCopyBuffer` node, and write-only access to `GUIUtility.systemCopyBuffer` in U#.
 —
# Why Write-Only
Being aware of VRChat's concerns with general purpose input/output (GPIO) from the VRC client, write-only access would require user-intervention to write back ("paste") clipboard contents in any particular world, and would be restricted to doing so in UI Input Fields and *re-implementations* thereof.
 
**Likewise**, write only access **prevents random-access of the user clipboard**, *which poses a security risk in the event the clipboard contains sensitive content.*
 —
# Further considerations
**If random-write access is of a concern, the Udon implementation could provide a mandatory UI dialog prompting the user if they wish to to copy text to the clipboard.**
E.G. "*Do you wish to copy "Some random text that will be truncated..." [509 Characters] to the clipboard?*" with "`Cancel`" & "`Copy`" options.
**Likewise, a variable indicating the copy's success could be provided, allowing udon developers to handle copy failure.**
E.G. `GUIUtility set systemCopyBuffer` will return a bool indicating the success (true) or failure (false) based on whether the user copied or canceled the action.
title: Add Write-Only Access to Clipboard (systemCopyBuffer)

details:
As it stands, the ability for developers to apply occlusion culling to udon scripts themselves is fairly limited. There are many cases where behaviors, such as those ran in `Update`/`LateUpdate`/`FixedUpdate`, **are not necessary when the objects attached are not in view**.
 —
# Example
A developer adds a "scrubber" to a video player, with time display via text on both sides. Once per second (done by collecting the `time` during each `LateUpdate` and comparing it to a copy of the time stored during the last update), the udon behavior pulls the current time of the video, the length of the video, applies these to the scrubber, then runs a series of floors and multiplication & division to the time and max time before formatting them into a string for a HH:MM:SS time display.
The entirety of this behavior is only necessary when the controls are actively within view of the player, and could be safely culled.
Another developer has a game world. They are looking for a way to have an NPC move and act when the viewer is not facing the NPC. By providing the option to register the NPC's visibility, when the player looks away (and no camera is in view) the NPC's specified udon behaviors will engage, until such a time that the player or a camera looks at them again.
 —
# Request
Add support for the [OnBecameInvisible](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/MonoBehaviour.OnBecameInvisible.html) & [OnBecameVisible](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/MonoBehaviour.OnBecameVisible.html) events.
 —
# Additional Note
In reading, for some there is confusion with these events, as Unity's behavior **purportedly includes Editor views, including the Scene view, even when inactive, in determining visibility.** If true, documentation should note that for successful testing in-editor, the scene view should be pointed **away** from the object which behavior is being tested.
 —
# Related Feedback
- [OnBecameInvisible, OnBecameVisible, broken](https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/onbecameinvisible-onbecamevisible-broken)
title: Add support for OnBecameVisible & OnBecameInvisible

Currently, key elements of World experience are completely out of control of creators. Users should retain final control over most of these settings for safety and accessibility reasons, but World creators need better tools for guiding users for the best experience in their World.
I suggest a prompt upon joining a World (default disabled in the SDK) that advises the user of the best settings for the World, formatted as an approval dialogue so that users don't need to navigate their menu. This is analogous to how web browsers and phone apps will request certain permissions in context, via prompt.
The world's requested settings should automatically revert to the user's previous settings upon leaving the world.
The included image shows an example. World creators could include some or all of these requests, or others.
I invite others to comment below with other settings that might be good to be requestable by a world creator. For now, I think the three most important are:
- World volume level. Hard cap this request to 70%.
- Earmuff mode off
- Nameplates On or Off
title: Allow Worlds to request important settings configurations

details:
Hi, I've found a bug in the Udon Graph compiler to do with merging/combining flows within the same Event.
See the picture of the graph labeled "A". The program will always flow into the False branch, then it should log Counter, increment Counter by 1, and then log it again. So if Counter starts at 0, it should print 0 then 1. However, the program actually just prints 0 and 0 again.
Compare that to the graph labeled "B", which should have exactly the same behavior -- all that changed was moving a flow to another set of identical nodes. And, moreover, the flow that was changed never even gets executed because the program will always take the False branch. However, with program "B", the program now has the correct behavior of printing 0 then 1.
I've attached an picture of an annotated side by side comparison of the compiled Udon Assembly for each of these programs. The "good" case ("B") is on the left, and the "bad" case ("A") is on the right. See that the code is identical -- except for a missing 4 instructions for the increment on the "bad" case.
Basically, it seems the compiler is assuming the flows exiting a Branch node will never merge back together, which isn't true. I'm a little confused about what the compiler is actually trying to do right now... the False case somehow gets both Logs, but misses the addition. But regardless, the solution will require figuring out the point at which the flows merge back together and having both True and False cases end by JUMPing to that instruction.
Thanks!
title: Merging flows after Branch generates incorrect Udon Assembly

Reproduction:

2. Put the Udon to object.
3. Do `Build & Test` and run 2 or more clients.
4. After every clients are in the instance, close one client that is current object owner.
5. Observe the result.
Expected results: Leaving the current owner fires `OnOwnershipTransferred()` on other clients so the clients can detect owner changing.
Actual results: Leaving the current owner does not fire `OnOwnershipTransferred()` on other clients, and its owner is silently changed.
---
Picture 1: Event log by the joining player. The last owner leaves after getting the owner with SetOwner. The event is fired to the joining player.

details:
On Later-Joiner's client, synced variables can be changed and OnVariableChanged will be fired without `OnDeserialization()` before `Start()` at the specific situation. Then usual `OnDeserialization()` will fire that causes desynchronization between the object owner.
The specific situation is: The Owner uses `RequestSerialization()` at `OnPlayerJoined()` or within some frames later, and The Later-Joiner is the first instance in its client.
(otherwise, it won't happened)
It can be critical problem because it makes `Start()` is not be guaranteed before any Udon events: firing `OnVariableChanged` before `Start()` can break Udons that implementing initialization at `Start()`.
----
I've created the world for reproduction. Tested on local build, but couldn't test for remote.
World URL : https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_f7f64709-5f9c-44f5-9f89-f63c9346c15f
World Mechanics: Front UI is main console. Joining a player increases synced int.
Sync timing is different between 4 consoles. (upper-left: Nothing, upper-right: Start only, lower-left: OnPlayerJoined only, lower-right: Both)
----
Reproduction:
1. Join above world (called Player A) this could be later instances in Player A's client.
2. Check log message about `Sync_JoinCount`.
3. Another player join same instance (called Player B). The player MUST use the first instance in Player B's client (Use direct link!!).
4. Check log message about `Sync_JoinCount`.
Expected Results:
At Player B log, Value Change log should be after `Start()` log.
Actual Results:
At Player B log, Value Change log happens before `Start()` log. (Picture is in local build test)
(If the instance is not the first in Player B's client, expected result will happen.)
----
Build: 1259
SDK World: 3.1.10
title: [1259] Synced variables can be changed from owner's `RequestSerialization()` before Later-Joiner's `Start()` at specific situation.

details:
Udon World Hand Gestures or Capacitive Buttons

Current there is no way for Udon to know what gesture a given player is making with their hand. 

If avatar gestures were to be exposed to Udon for the purpose of using them for world events triggers, world builder could use player hand gestures to interact with the world. In addition, combining player's Avatar hand gestures with the motion and position of the hand can allow for an infinite amount of interesting world interactions. 

For example a player could hold their open hand gesture out in front of them to create and energy shield, and make a fist gesture and punch forward to create an energy blast of varying power depending on the velocity of the controller's movement. 

We do have access to thumb stick positions, triggers and grip buttons presses, and A, B, X, Y button presses but do not have access to capacitive button touch which some gestures rely on. Allowing Udon to access capacitive buttons will allow world builders to create systems that could mimic the VRChat gesture system, but the best solution would be to send the given gestures straight through from player avatar to world Udon.

Thank you,

Zorgy
title: Udon World Hand Gestures or Capacitive Buttons

details:
# Issue:

Currently it's not possible to react to a players voice at all. We don't know when someone is talking or how loud they are for example. This limits us from making games where someone needs to be quiet to hide from an enemy for example.

For security reasons it makes sense that we can't just listen to a player voice, which is why I think only giving limited access to it would be fine.

# Suggestion:

Add an `isTalking` bool to the VRC Player API which is true when voice is detected and false when not.

Add a `loudness` float to the VRC Player API which is a value between 0 and 1 depending on how loud a player is. (Basically how the current Voice parameter works on Avatars)

Add a `viseme` integer to the VRC Player API which would indicate what viseme is currently used. (Basically how the current Viseme parameter works on Avatars)

These would allow world creators to integrate player voice into game play while also not just directly giving them access to player voices for security.
title: Player Voice variables for Udon (e.g. isTalking, loudness, viseme)

details:
This is from some reading of the SDK DLLs, it is not validated, but you may wanna double check:

Reading through `MidiRawDataProcessor()`, there are a couple bugs in parsing out blocks here in the Midi on/off block processing:

First, the noteTime dictionary is being accessed without a check if an item exists within the `MidiOff` processing - so if a `MidiOff` event appears when no `MidiOn` event has yet appeared, the processor will crash. There is a check, however it occurs after this access, which includes a member access of the start time and start velocity. This check does throw an exception, but it's a much more useful one - `note off event - could not find matching on event`.

This also occurs in the case of an `[On, Off, Off]` sequence.

Secondly, in the case of an equal but overlapping amount, say `[On, On, Off, Off]`, the result will be that the first On is ignored and will instead create 2 blocks which start at the second On but at the given Off currently being processed. The exact way you want to handle this is undefined I believe, but imo you should not be disposing of the first On event here regardless. See the last part for a potential fix.

Lastly, you've got an unused `this.allBlocks` member variable - why I bring this up is this actually has some (but not all) of the logic to do the above correctly - though it seems like you tried to update Velocity and StartTimeMs to the old event, which would fix #2 - except you've already overwritten that data, so the operation is redundant aside from the Count - 1. See the last part for a potential fix.

In general, the solution I see here is to keep a list of `NoteOn` events to feed to `NoteOff` events in your dictionary's value (or however you decide to structure it) to use as a queue (FIFO vs LIFO doesn't matter, this is unspecified in the MIDI standard afaik) instead of just keeping the latest value, and move the proper checks for this above the construction of `midiBlock` in processing your `NoteOff` event to avoid an NPE/null ref member access.
title: Bugs + potential crash in MidiRawDataProcessor

details:
With the Remote string loading and image loading, we should be able to dynamically construct endpoint url's to cater to different scenarios and offer more flexibility.

I know other posts about this do exist, but I feel like VRChat won't really pay attention without there being more volume and input from the end users. Please upvote relevant requests and share your thoughts. I'm using this post to potentially share my feedback and idea, and offer a starting point for us to discuss on. I want to be able to kickoff my project in VRChat and the string loading with dynamic URL's will play a major role in making it a reality.

I am assuming this was not possible because of "security" concerns, but let's face it that we offer users to block untrusted URL's as is and give them warnings.

VRChat is not only a social platform, but a sandbox for creators in terms of avatar, world, and scripting content.

I've developed essential tools on Garry's Mod and other sandbox games, and they had no problem letting scripts make API calls, despite the community having a dangerous and toxic userbase. This allowed me to let my clients configure "roles" and preferences from an external web portal.

Are you afraid of data exfiltration? There are ways to do that already.

Malicious URL calls? Anything on the internet can be malicious as is. We can't keep having this "Carebear" security mindset and keep it locked tight that severely limits our creativity, but look for accountability and flexibility. The security concern is admired, but now its necessary to send dynamic URL's for search queries when we deal with remote strings or images, otherwise we have no choice but to dump the entire dataset.

I will just have to create hundreds of VRCURL's and just do a bunch of if/else's and download the entire "database" instead of feeding search queries to get specific datasets to save bandwidth and filter through the data set on the server side.

Maybe to meet in the middle, we can be transparent of the requests to be made. Add a prompt to the end user stating that "This World is requesting permission to let your game send/receive content to and from http://xyz.com" and it would be whitelisted to that user individually. Any new URL's not on the list will prompt another permission request. It would **Only** apply to the domain name, and Subdomain only. Maybe prevent changing the domain/subdomain of the URL entirely. This can also allow the user to feel more confidence knowing that their "Untrusted URLs" is no longer a wildcard, but can consult a list to see which untrusted URL's they're permitting on their client.

With your upcoming "Udon" menu implementation, it could be considered to have VRChat built-in user preferences specific to the worlds, and include the whitelist there of URLs the World has requested to communicate with.
title: Allow VRCURL URL / Dynamic URLs At Runtime, It's Time for a Change

details:
Objects spawned from a VRC Object Pool no longer call `OnDeserialization()` for late joiners.  

Objects get spawned by the pool and placed in the world by the user, after that, `RequestSerialization()` is called. (So it is not related to this [issue](https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/1287-ondeserialization-no-longer-being-called-on-manual-synced-objects-unless-re))  

It properly runs and syncs with people already in the world.  

Late joiners now will run `Start()` (which, a year ago object pool objects did not run `Start()` or `OnEnable()`, that got fixed now) but never `OnDeserialization()`.  

  

A current workaround is: the `Start()` is called very late and has the variables synced already, so any placement logic can go in there, but that requires updating old worlds.  

The documentation says, any networked object is calling `OnDeserialization()` for late joiners, which it doesn't in this case.
title: [1287] OnDeserialization no longer called for late joiners for manual synced objects spawned from VRC Object Pool

details:
Integer fields in json data are being stored as Doubles in DataToken when using VRCJson.TryDeserializeFromJson in Udon#

Example Code:

```

DataToken data;

string json = "{ \"MyInt\": 12345 }";

if(VRCJson.TryDeserializeFromJson(json, out data))

{

    Debug.Log("Int" + ((DataDictionary)data)["MyInt"].Int.ToString());

}

```

causes exception:

```

[UdonSharp] Assets/JsonTest.cs(29,61): Udon runtime exception detected!

  An exception occurred during EXTERN to 'VRCSDK3DataDataToken.__get_Int__SystemInt32'.

      Parameter Addresses: 0x00000024, 0x00000025

  Attempted to access Double token as Int

```

Recommend parsing the json data correctly or providing getters/casts with auto type conversion.

Casts would be the preferable auto type conversion.

While getters like .Int .Double .Float would throw if the type mismatches

If I'm casting, I'm expecting the type to cast properly.

Doing an `(Int)((Double)(my_data_token))` is pretty dumb from a typecasting standpoint.

If casting an invalid format, like a dict/list to an int, then I would expect an exception.

strings I don't have a great opinion on. I think it would nice to run a Int64.Parse when casting a string to an int, but it would be acceptable to just throw a "cannot convert string to int" and expect the json to be formated properly
title: VRCJson.TryDeserializeFromJson stores Integers as Doubles

comments.body:
I understand the points that are being made.

But also realize that a double beyond 53 bits of mantissa can no longer represent all possible integers below it's maxim.

The utility of such large doubles is very low and is better served with custom math wrappers where passing the value as a string would be preferred for custom number parsing.

The JSON specification even calls out the range [-(2^53)+1, (2^53)-1] explicitly as a good interoperable range.

In this example precision is lost by treating the value as a double:

`Console.WriteLine ((long)(double)8000000000000000001);`

This code will output the value 8000000000000000000 because double does not actually have enough precision to store an int64

I shall accept the limitations imposed by the VRCJson implementation. but working with large values should be fully understood before imposing limitations on implementation.

If Doubles are meant to store int64's then they would need to have the precision available to store the in64 which they do not.

I just don't feel that values without an explicit decimal point should be treated as floating point where I can lose precision.

I will make due if the VRC Devs are not willing to budge on the matter. As I only intend my values to reach the millions and not get into the quintillions that something like IdleHome may reach with it's exponential value increases.

Thank you for the explanation on the design choices.

@{60285ca04963ba22994f485b|full_name}: Or it could be parsed as both a Double and an Int64 and the appropriate IsDouble/IsInt could return the status as to whether the value was parsed correctly, providing exception safety.

If the original value contains a decimal point then IsInt would return false as the value is obviously not intended to be an integer.

This is really basic stuff and unless the implementation under the hood is written in C99 using the union type I can't see why an implementation like this wasn't considered. Or perhaps it was?

TokenType can become Number and IsInt/IsDouble can be used to determine the type of number, and as already stated double will cover all the numerical types for those lazy enough to only want to do if (token.IsNumber) then token.Double.

And for those that need int64 precision they can do if (token.IsNumber && token.IsInt) then token.Int

As for the issue with converting a token that contains both a double and integer representation when being converted back into JSON, a simple if (IntPart > 9007199254740992 || IntPart < -9007199254740992) then write the integer value, otherwise write the decimal

@{6224733347335c0452995113|full_name}: I understand that this is frustrating, but it's a limitation of storing values in strings without specifying the data type. There's only so much that you can assume, and there's only so much you can do. If it's any consolation, we are planning to release an update adding byte array serialization in the future, which will preserve both the data type and values much more accurately, while also taking up less space than JSON. This is the real solution to your problem.

@{6224733347335c0452995113|full_name}: DataTokens cannot contain two values at the same time. Once it's been requested, it needs to decide what type it is. Automatically picking a different type depending on what the value is would cause other issues, like TryGetValue<Double> returning false because the type isn't what you expect.

details:
# Details

Currently, there is no way to listen to the *arbitrary* entry of a station by a player. This results in additional overhead and workload, requiring an Udon behaviour on every station which needs to respond to this event, which both risks performance decreases and generates undue developer workload in worst-case scenarios.

# Feature Request

Provide `OnPlayerStationEntered(VRCPlayerApi player, VRCStation station)` and `OnPlayerStationExited(VRCPlayerApi player, VRCStation station)` as global events which can be listened to via udon.

Similar to other `OnPlayer` events, these would be triggered by the player's actions/state, as opposed to any particular event on a particular object. By this method, developers, when needed, can work with stations *arbitrarily*, such as for setting the height of a station based on a slider, manipulating arbitrary station properties, and working with stations in a complex manner from a singular Udon behaviour, whilst avoiding duplicate code, scripts, or messy distributed script setups.
title: Provide OnPlayerStationEntered and OnPlayerStationExited to Udon

Worlds have already shown amazing concepts that are possible with desyncing player positions, but they require that everyone is constantly in a station, syncs their position and has a custom moving controller which adds a lot of overhead. 

It would be great if a player doesn't need to enter a station themselves to be in one remotely, so new concepts of desynced positions are possible, which would be great e.g. for games where one player is supposed to be invisible to some other players, but they themselves can walk around others freely.

details:
Currently VRCJson.TryDeserializeFromJson and VRCJson.TrySerializeToJson have two big limitations :

- DataDictionary keys need to be strings.

- `Int`s are converted into `Double`.

Those limitations forces anyone who wants to sync the DataDictitonary to work with strings as keys, and to use `double`s instead of `int`:

- In the first case, keys need to be converted into strings, which could cause issues if someone need to call `GetKeys().Sort()` to get a sorted key/value pair list, keys need to be converted into numerical values first, which is a bit annoying.

- In the second case, all numerical values needs to be converted into double, which can cause errors and bugs if the creator forgot to use `double` instead of `int`, just as an example would be storing player IDs (that are `int`s), so IDs need to be casted into `double` beforehand.

My suggestion would be to add an option to also serialize the data type of the DataToken, the outputed JSON could look like this 

```

 {

 	"Int:0": "String:value1",

 	"Int:1": "String:value2"

 }

```

instead of 

```

{

 	"0": "value1",

 	"1": "value2"

 }

```

 this would make the string longer, but it would allow to serialize a wider range of data types. Maybe adding a new `JsonExportType` value like `JsonExportType.WithTypes` ?
title: Currently VRCJson.TrySerializeToJson and VRCJson.TryDeserializeFromJson have a few limitations, add an option to also serialize the data type

There is zero documentation on how the outline is even generated right now, so we can only guess and hope.

Often times VRChat takes the pickup outline not from the attached collider, but from a random sub mesh. At the same time, the "selectable area" of a pickup is taken from the collider instead. This results in a counter-intuitive outline that doesn't match the expected grabbing area.

Solution: We should be able to set the outlines ourselves so that it matches our desired outline. Ideally by assigning a mesh to the Pickup component.

We should also be able to change this visible outline at runtime (via Udon) by assigning a different mesh when needed. This is needed for any pickup that can change its shape, e.g. a book that can be opened or closed.

We should also be able to disable the outline entirely. People are already using PhysBones on Avatars to have "Pickups" that don't have an outline, so worlds should be able to do the same when needed.

There are some other requests related to Pickups that are as old as Udon, but are worth being mentioned here:

We should also be able to disable "drop", so the pickup stays in the player's hand. Similar to how you can "disable exit" on a station. There are countless games where the player needs to hold an item the entire time and never drop it, and actually needing to hold it yourself is not very nice.

details:
This is a feature I have been wondering about for some time now, and am curious as to whether it is a topic the VRChat developers would even remotely consider.

I propose adding some kind of deferred downloading system for worlds, in which a worlds developer can add a specific SDK component to a gameobject, or some similar system. This system would then cause that gameobjects children, and unique assets associated with them, to be packed into their own unique asset bundle, which is then uploaded alongside the main bundle to the servers. When the world is loaded, only the “main” asset bundle is downloaded before the player can enter. The main asset bundle can include whatever is not packaged in one of these custom-defined bundles, as well as any assets that are used by more than one bundle.

World creators would then have access to those “deferred download” components at runtime, and using Udon we would be able to request that the game download the predefined bundle created at upload time, and then insert it into the scene.

I am well aware that VRChat is focused on security and is not the biggest fan of allowing world maintainers to create arbitrary requests – I specifically ask not that we can control what gets downloaded at runtime, only *when* a certain thing is downloaded. 

This, alongside pre-downloading (which is beyond this post’s scope) would greatly decrease loading times as worlds would only have to download what is needed, rather than the entire world. This would also work well for worlds which make heavy use of exclusive content. Why wait longer at the loading screen to download all that content if you aren’t meant to see it?

This could be made even better if users could somehow use this feature for delta-updates to worlds, but I see that as even less likely :P Also, if there are concerns about this being used to circumvent the Quest world size limitation, I think the SDK could just calculate the total size of all asset bundles to see if its beyond the limit.

(I even have an, albeit poor, example of what this could look like to an end user here: https://i.gyazo.com/c63d42ca524d65fd6d09d7efe346e830.mp4)
title: Consider adding a deferred downloading system for worlds

details:
Gravity and Kinematic flags on `VRCObjectSync` components don't sync correctly right now and also cannot be set correctly while holding the pickup.

To set gravity or kinematic flags, VRChat added two new methods for us: https://udonsharp.docs.vrchat.com/vrchat-api/#vrcobjectsync (they are supposed to behave like a synced variable)

There are two bugs related to this:

~ **Bug 1: ** ~

All you need is to create a pickup that has no gravity and then toggle the gravity flag on the `VRCObjectSync` component with an external button after claiming ownership. Then you let different people in the world pick up the pickup and drop it (to show their own local state). In my tests, this resulted in a pickup where the gravity flag is wildly different on each client and only syncs occasionally or not at all. They would see the pickup drop on my end, but when they pick it up it has no gravity for them.

~ **Bug 2: ** ~

All you need is to create a pickup that has no gravity and then toggle the gravity flag on the `VRCObjectSync` component in `OnPickupUseDown()`. In my tests, this resulted in a pickup where the gravity stays enabled after the first `OnPickupUseDown()` and I am unable to turn gravity off again. To check gravity, the pickup is dropped.

You can also just test it out here:

Right setup: Bug 1 / Left setup: Bug 2

https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_9cefd5ec-4492-43c5-8cd3-05036c494556

Additional note: Since we only got a setter and not a getter method, we are left in the dark here when it comes to analyzing the problem. Reading out the local rigidbody state doesn't give us access to the real synced state. A getter method should be added.
title: VRCObjectSync doesn't sync Gravity/Kinematic flags reliably

comments.body: Thank you for reporting the issue!
Had a lot of problems in the past with gravity/kinematic sync and didn't really know what was going on. Looks like this is the cause of it, ty for posting it!

You're not alone in finding this issue! I have objects that need to appear as if they were destroyed, freezing in place, but when they respawn gravity doesn't reliably get restored as it should every time. No ownership issues since everyone receives the network call for it. Works only 95% of the time, but when it breaks it's really obvious and comes across as I'm crazy for trusting ObjectSync's gravity and/or kinetic syncing. Since making and toggling the script of my own local only gravity via a Force on a FixedUpdate(), the issue went away. ObjectSync still works like a charm with only the Network Owner having local gravity enabled. I imagine this isn't feasible or ideal for most scenarios though as there's a much larger performance impact in doing so, but this also felt like it proved something is wrong/unreliable with ObjectSync.

details:
While working on a world with a large VRCUrl array, I noticed VRChat's memory usage ballooned quickly upon rejoining the world multiple times.

I've put together a test world that shows this behavior. To make the behavior more apparent, it contains an unrealistic 2 million+ URLs that are each 64 characters long: https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_9029bdaf-6d58-4b3d-8c1e-ad6c8d4149e5

Upon joining this world immediately after starting VRChat, VRChat's memory usage is ~3.8GiB. Upon subsequent rejoins, it quickly approaches ~6.7GiB, and hovers around there for several rejoins before jumping to ~7.2GiB, ~7.7GiB, etc.

I rejoined enough times to hit ~8.6GiB.

I'm hesitant to call this a memory leak as it could just be heap/garbage collection related, but the RAM usage stays high even when leaving to go to a lighter world.

In general, I've found rejoining a "normal" world a dozen times in a row only sees a memory increase of a few dozen megabytes at most, so I still believe there is something odd going on here even if it's not a true memory leak.
title: [1345] Ballooning memory usage upon rejoining world with large VRCUrl arrays

Currently in order to achieve the same behaviour as a ternary operator, you have to add a new variable to the graph, branch your flow based on a boolean, set the value of the aforementioned variable, then merge the two flows together afterwards and get the variable value.

An even more version of the Select node would be if, given an integer or enum, it could evaluate and return the value of one of its inputs, from an array of inputs. This would act similarly to a switch statement which only returns a value based on the provided integer/enum. A good reference would be the UE Blueprints Select node, as it supports all of these selection types: Bool, Integer and Enum.

details: If you can just call SendNetworkEvent() after receiving OnPlayerTriggerEnter() to make it non-local, then why is this method not exclusively local? I cannot overstate how serious this issue is, especially for world optimization. The current implementation where IsLocal is checked AFTER the event is raised creates a potentially huge amount of network traffic for something that is almost never needed to be synced. When this method is used for optimizations (turning parts of a world on and off in ways that Unity's built-in tools cannot), a missed event for this is catastrophic. It would be far better to have a late event, or even multiple copies of it received because that can actually be handled programmatically, but when this event misses, it's probably among the worst failure modes it can have short of crashing the game or lagging out, if you think about it.
title: OnPlayerTriggerEnter()/Exit() is unreliable

details:
Since build 1344, teleporting the local player using their own rotation produces unexpected results:

```

Networking.LocalPlayer.TeleportTo(somePosition, Networking.LocalPlayer.GetRotation(), VRC_SceneDescriptor.SpawnOrientation.AlignPlayerWithSpawnPoint, true); 

```

Instead of keeping their exact orientation (as one would expect), the player can be rotated significantly depending on where the player is looking and when the teleport method was executed. 

When executing the teleport from Update(), the teleport can rotate a VR player but not a desktop player. If the player's head is mostly horizontal the teleport will not rotate the player. If the player looks down or up, they will be rotated randomly to the left or right. The farther their line of sight is from horizontal, the more they get rotated with looking straight down seemingly causing a 180 degree rotation. 

If the GetRotation and TeleportTo methods get executed during LateUpdate, the player always rotates by a large amount regardless of where the player is looking and whether they are in VR or not.

Additionally, if the player is in a generic avatar, they will not get rotated and the teleport works as expected.

This is especially useful for currency-like values, such as livestream donations.

details:
This topic might have been discussed before, though I couldn't seem to find any similar titles. The closest one I found in terms of disabling components on avatars in worlds would be this one (but it only talks about avatar stations): https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/allow-world-creators-of-sdk3-worlds-to-disable-stations-on-avatars

As it says in the title, I think world creators should be given the ability to disable certain components on an avatar. More specifically, any use of a Collider (not trigger) or Light(s), as these have often been used to gain some sort of unfair advantage in game worlds, especially when it comes to speed and height.

It'd be very beneficial for such worlds to blacklist these kinds of components, since the world creator doesn't have to make additional changes in an attempt to remove this kind of advantage. Scripts that are written to monitor this type of cheating aren't perfect by any means, as there could be false-positives, player circumventions, or some strange edge-case that wasn't caught beforehand. It'd just be one less problem to worry about if we could control which avatar components are allowed in a world.

I understand this might be a bit of a controversial feature for some people, since it would break intended functionality of some avatars. And I can understand that if you're in a private instance on your own or with others, why would it matter if you use an avatar like that at all? You're just there to have fun. But if automated saving/loading (or maybe even global leaderboards) ever become a built-in feature within VRChat, then it just seems unfair to the others that simply played by the rules.

Also, yes, I know: Playspace Mover is a thing that people use as well, but that isn't something that can be disabled. However, this one is a bit easier to mitigate and doesn't lift the player's capsule collider off the ground.
title: Allow world creators to blacklist specific avatar components
